ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: Rind of 1 unwaxed lemon, removed in strips
Biscuits or fresh fruit, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a heat-resistant bowl, mix together the egg yolks, caster sugar, wine and the lemon rind. Place the bowl over a slightly simmering bain-marie and whisk vigorously by hand or with an electric whisk until the mixture becomes frothy and doubles in volume. The water shouldn’t touch the bottom of the bowl.

Remove the bowl from the bain-marie and whisk for another 30 seconds. Remove the lemon rind and serve immediately in cups or glasses. Pair with biscuits or fresh fruit. Serving suggestion This Italian cream can be served as an accompaniment or topping for puddings, rice desserts, poached fruit or ice cream.

recipes.searchText: Zabaglione Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 4 egg yolks 75g caster sugar 250ml dry white wine (or champagne) Rind of 1 unwaxed lemon, removed in strips Biscuits or fresh fruit, to serve In a heat-resistant bowl, mix together the egg yolks, caster sugar, wine and the lemon rind. Place the bowl over a slightly simmering bain-marie and whisk vigorously by hand or with an electric whisk until the mixture becomes frothy and doubles in volume. The water shouldn’t touch the bottom of the bowl. Remove the bowl from the bain-marie and whisk for another 30 seconds. Remove the lemon rind and serve immediately in cups or glasses. Pair with biscuits or fresh fruit. Serving suggestion This Italian cream can be served as an accompaniment or topping for puddings, rice desserts, poached fruit or ice cream.
recipes.title: Zabaglione

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200g mixed berries of your choice, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: The day before, prepare the almond milk: bring the measured water and ground almonds to the boil in a saucepan. Blend the mixture with a hand blender while still hot, then filter it using a fine mesh sieve, pressing down with a spatula to extract all the milk. Refrigerate overnight.
The following day, soften the gelatine sheets in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes, then drain.

In a small saucepan, heat a quarter of the almond milk. Add the bitter almond extract and gelatine sheets, mix well to melt them completely, then pour the contents of the saucepan into the rest of the almond milk and stir. Add the caster sugar and mix until dissolved.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, then carefully add it to the mixture using a rubber spatula. Pour this mixture into an 18cm round Charlotte cake tin or 4– 6 moulds and refrigerate for 4–5 hours.
Briefly submerge the tin or individual moulds in hot water, then flip the blancmange on to a serving dish. Decorate it with mixed berries before serving.

recipes.searchText: Blancmange Crèmes & mousses Ingredients For The Almond Milk 6 gelatine sheets 1 drop bitter almond extract 100g caster sugar 400ml cold whipping cream 200g mixed berries of your choice, to serve 250ml water 140g ground almonds The day before, prepare the almond milk: bring the measured water and ground almonds to the boil in a saucepan. Blend the mixture with a hand blender while still hot, then filter it using a fine mesh sieve, pressing down with a spatula to extract all the milk. Refrigerate overnight. recipes.title: Blancmange

ingredientGroups.heading: For The Coulis
lines: 400g red berries of your choice – one type or a mixture (strawberries, redcurrants, raspberries or wild strawberries)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soften the gelatine sheets by soaking them in a bowl of cold water for about 10 minutes.

Pour the coconut milk, cream and sugar into a saucepan. Split the vanilla pod lengthways and scrape out the seeds with a small knife. Add the seeds to the saucepan, mix well and bring the contents to the boil. Remove from the heat, cover and allow it to sit for a few minutes to infuse.
Drain the gelatine sheets, then add them to the saucepan. Mix well. Pour the mixture into 4 glasses and refrigerate for 4 hours.

Prepare the coulis: hull the strawberries and stem the redcurrants, if using. Pulse the fruit in a blender with the icing sugar, then strain using a fine mesh sieve. Thin the coulis with a little water if necessary (depending on the type of fruit used). Divide the coulis between the 4 glasses of panna cotta, decorate with red berries and serve cold.

recipes.searchText: Coconut and Red Berry Panna Cotta Crèmes & mousses Ingredients For The Coulis 3 gelatine sheets 200ml coconut milk 250ml single cream 50g caster sugar 1 vanilla pod 400g red berries of your choice – one type or a mixture (strawberries, redcurrants, raspberries or wild strawberries) 50g icing sugar Soften the gelatine sheets by soaking them in a bowl of cold water for about 10 minutes. Pour the coconut milk, cream and sugar into a saucepan. Split the vanilla pod lengthways and scrape out the seeds with a small knife. Add the seeds to the saucepan, mix well and bring the contents to the boil. Remove from the heat, cover and allow it to sit for a few minutes to infuse. Drain the gelatine sheets, then add them to the saucepan. Mix well. Pour the mixture into 4 glasses and refrigerate for 4 hours. Prepare the coulis: hull the strawberries and stem the redcurrants, if using. Pulse the fruit in a blender with the icing sugar, then strain using a fine mesh sieve. Thin the coulis with a little water if necessary (depending on the type of fruit used). Divide the coulis between the 4 glasses of panna cotta, decorate with red berries and serve cold.
recipes.title: Coconut and Red Berry Panna Cotta

ingredientGroups.heading: For The Caramel
lines: A few drops of lemon juice

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the rice pudding: split the vanilla pod in half lengthways. In a large, heavy-based saucepan, bring the milk, split vanilla pod, caster sugar and rice to the boil. Reduce the heat, cover and simmer very gently for 30–40 minutes. Once the rice is cooked, add the butter and stir, then leave to cool.

Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Remove the vanilla pod from the rice and add the egg yolks, mixing well. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt, then gradually fold them into the rice.

Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Prepare the caramel: pour the measured cold water and the caster sugar into a heavy-based saucepan. Add the lemon juice and boil over a high heat. Once the caramel starts to brown at the edges, gently and rhythmically swirl the saucepan to mix the contents. Once the caramel is golden, pour half of it into a 20cm fluted Charlotte tin, turning the tin in order to distribute the caramel evenly on all sides.
Reheat the rest of the caramel, add the measured hot water and boil for 2 minutes until liquid. Allow it to cool.
Pour the rice mixture into the tin and pack it in tightly. Place it in the oven in a bain-marie with very hot water. Bake for 45 minutes.
Allow the cake to cool, then remove it from the tin and place it on a serving dish. Pour the liquid caramel over.

recipes.searchText: Rice and Caramel Cake Crèmes & mousses For The Rice Pudding For The Caramel 1 vanilla pod 900ml whole milk 70g caster sugar 100g short-grain rice 50g butter 3 eggs A pinch of salt 4 tablespoons cold water 125g caster sugar A few drops of lemon juice 50ml hot water Prepare the rice pudding: split the vanilla pod in half lengthways. In a large, heavy-based saucepan, bring the milk, split vanilla pod, caster sugar and rice to the boil. Reduce the heat, cover and simmer very gently for 30–40 minutes. Once the rice is cooked, add the butter and stir, then leave to cool. Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Remove the vanilla pod from the rice and add the egg yolks, mixing well. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt, then gradually fold them into the rice. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Prepare the caramel: pour the measured cold water and the caster sugar into a heavy-based saucepan. Add the lemon juice and boil over a high heat. Once the caramel starts to brown at the edges, gently and rhythmically swirl the saucepan to mix the contents. Once the caramel is golden, pour half of it into a 20cm fluted Charlotte tin, turning the tin in order to distribute the caramel evenly on all sides. Reheat the rest of the caramel, add the measured hot water and boil for 2 minutes until liquid. Allow it to cool. Pour the rice mixture into the tin and pack it in tightly. Place it in the oven in a bain-marie with very hot water. Bake for 45 minutes. Allow the cake to cool, then remove it from the tin and place it on a serving dish. Pour the liquid caramel over.
recipes.title: Rice and Caramel Cake

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the citrus peel: remove the orange and grapefruit rinds without cutting into the pith. Chop into thin slivers. Submerge these in a saucepan of boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain. Change the water in the saucepan, bring it to the boil and repeat the process. Drain the citrus peel.

Slowly bring the measured water to the boil in a saucepan with the brown sugar, stirring until the sugar is completely dissolved. Submerge the citrus peel in this syrup, simmer for 10 minutes, then remove them with a slotted spoon. Let them cool before chopping them into small pieces.

Prepare the rice pudding: split the vanilla pod in half lengthways. In a large, heavy-based saucepan, bring the milk to the boil with the split vanilla pod, caster sugar and rice. Reduce the heat, cover and cook very gently for 30–40 minutes. Allow it to cool, then add the egg yolks. Mix well. Allow the mixture to cool completely.

Prepare the whipped cream: whip the cream to soft peaks. Carefully mix it in with the crystallized citrus peel (reserving some for decoration) and rice, then pour the dessert into a large bowl. Refrigerate until you’re ready to serve. Sprinkle with the reserved citrus peel pieces before serving.

Chop into thin slivers. Submerge these in a saucepan of boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain. Change the water in the saucepan, bring it to the boil and repeat the process. Drain the citrus peel. Slowly bring the measured water to the boil in a saucepan with the brown sugar, stirring until the sugar is completely dissolved. Submerge the citrus peel in this syrup, simmer for 10 minutes, then remove them with a slotted spoon. Let them cool before chopping them into small pieces. Prepare the rice pudding: split the vanilla pod in half lengthways. In a large, heavy-based saucepan, bring the milk to the boil with the split vanilla pod, caster sugar and rice. Reduce the heat, cover and cook very gently for 30–40 minutes. Allow it to cool, then add the egg yolks. Mix well. Allow the mixture to cool completely. Prepare the whipped cream: whip the cream to soft peaks. Carefully mix it in with the crystallized citrus peel (reserving some for decoration) and rice, then pour the dessert into a large bowl. Refrigerate until you’re ready to serve. Sprinkle with the reserved citrus peel pieces before serving.
recipes.title: Citrus Rice Pudding

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the almond milk and agave syrup in a small saucepan. Once the mixture is hot, add the tapioca pearls and cook over a very low heat for about 20 minutes, until the tapioca become translucent and the mixture has thickened.
Toast the almonds in a frying pan.

Remove the tapioca from the heat and carefully add the raspberries and flaked almonds to the saucepan, reserving some of each for decoration. Pour the cream mixture into small glasses and refrigerate for 3 hours. Just before serving, sprinkle the reserved flaked almonds and raspberries on top. ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: A drizzle of orange blossom water

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soften the raisins in the orange blossom water. Heat the milk with 100g of the sugar, then pour in the semolina flour all at once and whisk without stopping until the mixture has thickened. Beat the eggs and add them to the semolina. Mix in the raisins and orange blossom water.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Heat the remaining sugar in a saucepan with a few drops of water, then allow it to caramelize. Pour the caramel into a 22cm Charlotte mould, ensuring it coats the sides.
Pour in the semolina mixture and bake for 20 minutes. Let the cake cool, then remove it from the tin.

recipes.searchText: Orange and Raisin Semolina Cake Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 70g raisins A drizzle of orange blossom water 1 litre whole milk 190g caster sugar 135g fine semolina flour 3 eggs Soften the raisins in the orange blossom water. Heat the milk with 100g of the sugar, then pour in the semolina flour all at once and whisk without stopping until the mixture has thickened. Beat the eggs and add them to the semolina. Mix in the raisins and orange blossom water. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Heat the remaining sugar in a saucepan with a few drops of water, then allow it to caramelize. Pour the caramel into a 22cm Charlotte mould, ensuring it coats the sides. Pour in the semolina mixture and bake for 20 minutes. Let the cake cool, then remove it from the tin.
recipes.title: Orange and Raisin Semolina Cake

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F), Gas Mark 7. In an ovenproof saucepan, heat the milk with the caster sugar, vanilla pod and a pinch of salt. Add the rice and butter, stir and slowly bring to the boil. Cover, then place the saucepan in the oven and cook for 25–30 minutes.
Meanwhile, separate the egg whites from the yolks. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks.
Remove the pan from the oven and gently stir in the egg yolks one by one. Then slowly incorporate the egg whites.

Reduce the oven temperature to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease a 22cm round tin (or 6–8 ovenproof ramekins, about 8–10cm in diameter) and sprinkle with breadcrumbs. Pour the mixture into the tin or ramekins, place in a bain-marie and bake for 30–35 minutes (20–25 minutes for the ramekins). Serving suggestion This pudding can be served with a mixed berry coulis.

recipes.searchText: Rice Pudding Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 1 litre milk 100g caster sugar ½ vanilla pod A pinch of salt 150g short-grain rice 50g butter + extra for greasing 6 eggs 30g fine breadcrumbs Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F), Gas Mark 7. In an ovenproof saucepan, heat the milk with the caster sugar, vanilla pod and a pinch of salt. Add the rice and butter, stir and slowly bring to the boil. Cover, then place the saucepan in the oven and cook for 25–30 minutes. Meanwhile, separate the egg whites from the yolks. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks. Remove the pan from the oven and gently stir in the egg yolks one by one. Then slowly incorporate the egg whites. Reduce the oven temperature to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease a 22cm round tin (or 6–8 ovenproof ramekins, about 8–10cm in diameter) and sprinkle with breadcrumbs. Pour the mixture into the tin or ramekins, place in a bain-marie and bake for 30–35 minutes (20–25 minutes for the ramekins). Serving suggestion This pudding can be served with a mixed berry coulis.
recipes.title: Rice Pudding

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water for 5–10 minutes. Meanwhile, using an electric mixer, whip the cold cream to soft peaks. Mix the raspberries with the icing sugar.
Squeeze out the gelatine and place in the microwave for 20 seconds, to melt. Mix it into the raspberry coulis.

Gently mix the whipped cream with the raspberry coulis and divide between individual serving cups or bowls. Cool for at least 2 hours in the fridge. Just before serving, decorate with fresh raspberries.

recipes.searchText: Raspberry Mousse Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 2 gelatine sheets 150ml cold whipping cream 200g raspberries + extra for decorating 80g icing sugar Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water for 5–10 minutes. Meanwhile, using an electric mixer, whip the cold cream to soft peaks. Mix the raspberries with the icing sugar. Squeeze out the gelatine and place in the microwave for 20 seconds, to melt. Mix it into the raspberry coulis. Gently mix the whipped cream with the raspberry coulis and divide between individual serving cups or bowls. Cool for at least 2 hours in the fridge. Just before serving, decorate with fresh raspberries.
recipes.title: Raspberry Mousse

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Finely grate the zest from the limes. Cut the limes in half, juice them and pour the juice into a saucepan.
Separate the egg whites from the yolks.

Add the caster sugar and lime zest to the saucepan (reserving some zest for decoration) and slowly bring to the boil. When the first bubbles appear, remove the saucepan from the heat and pour its contents on to the egg yolks, whisking vigorously. Return the mixture to the saucepan and slowly heat it, stirring continuously until thickened. Remove from the heat and allow it to cool.
Whip the cold cream into firm peaks until it sticks to the whisk. Add the icing sugar, mix well and carefully fold into the lime cream.
Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with a pinch of salt. Carefully fold them into the prepared mixture, scooping as you stir so the mousse doesn’t deflate.
Pour into a large bowl or into 6 smaller bowls. Refrigerate for 4 hours. Serve cold, decorated with the reserved lime zest.

recipes.searchText: Lime Mousse Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 4 unwaxed limes 6 eggs 100g caster sugar 500ml cold whipping cream 100g icing sugar A pinch of salt Finely grate the zest from the limes. Cut the limes in half, juice them and pour the juice into a saucepan. Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Add the caster sugar and lime zest to the saucepan (reserving some zest for decoration) and slowly bring to the boil. When the first bubbles appear, remove the saucepan from the heat and pour its contents on to the egg yolks, whisking vigorously. Return the mixture to the saucepan and slowly heat it, stirring continuously until thickened. Remove from the heat and allow it to cool. Whip the cold cream into firm peaks until it sticks to the whisk. Add the icing sugar, mix well and carefully fold into the lime cream. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with a pinch of salt. Carefully fold them into the prepared mixture, scooping as you stir so the mousse doesn’t deflate. Pour into a large bowl or into 6 smaller bowls. Refrigerate for 4 hours. Serve cold, decorated with the reserved lime zest.
recipes.title: Lime Mousse

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 large, ripe bananas, peeled and sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Juice the lime and drizzle it over the banana slices. Blend the bananas with the mascarpone and cinnamon until finely puréed.

In a large bowl, whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt, adding the sugar halfway through. Continue whipping until the egg whites become firm and velvety. Use a rubber spatula to fold them into the purée carefully.

Divide the mousse between 4 small bowls and refrigerate for 1 hour. Serve cold. Serving suggestion The mousse can be enjoyed on its own or, depending on the season, with a salad of exotic fruits or mixed red berries.

recipes.searchText: Cinnamon and Banana Mousse Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 1 unwaxed lime 4 large, ripe bananas, peeled and sliced 60g mascarpone ⅓ teaspoon ground cinnamon 3 egg whites A pinch of salt 50g caster sugar Juice the lime and drizzle it over the banana slices. Blend the bananas with the mascarpone and cinnamon until finely puréed. In a large bowl, whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt, adding the sugar halfway through. Continue whipping until the egg whites become firm and velvety. Use a rubber spatula to fold them into the purée carefully. Divide the mousse between 4 small bowls and refrigerate for 1 hour. Serve cold. Serving suggestion The mousse can be enjoyed on its own or, depending on the season, with a salad of exotic fruits or mixed red berries.
recipes.title: Cinnamon and Banana Mousse

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Folding in the egg whites Start by mixing a quarter of the whipped egg whites into the mixture to soften it. Put some energy into the whisking. Add the rest of the egg whites in two or three stages with a spatula, folding from the centre of the bowl and moving toward the edges. Stop folding once there are no more visible egg whites or the mixture may begin to lose volume. 2 well distributed filling Many cook books recommend adding flour when adding raisins, but this doesn’t really make a difference. What does work, is to incorporate a filling (dried fruit, fruit pieces, chocolate chips) into the batter, then allow it to rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator. Next transfer the batter into the greased and floured tin and bake immediately. As it bakes, the batter will start to set before the fruit has time to sink to the bottom.

A successful Chantilly cream The fat content in cream is what makes Chantilly set: it’s imperative that you opt for whipping cream with a 30–35 per cent fat content. It also needs to be very cold, as does the bowl. Place it in the freezer 15 minutes before use. For an even firmer Chantilly that is dense and holds well, add a little mascarpone (which has a fat content of about 60 per cent): use 1 heaped tablespoon for 300–500ml of cream. Whip everything in a very cold bowl. Once whipped, the cream will keep its texture for about 2 hours in the refrigerator. Whipped cream or Chantilly cream? Whipped cream is whipping cream that has been whisked to incorporate air. It’s plain instead of sweet and is often added to other preparations, such as mousses. Chantilly cream is a sweet whipped cream, which is used most often as a topping for desserts.

Rounded madeleines To give your madeleines a nice rounded shape, prepare the batter the day before and keep it refrigerated overnight, or for at least 2 hours. Grease your madeleine tins before pouring in the batter and quickly put them in the oven. The madeleines will rise because of the sudden change in temperature between the cold batter and the hot oven.

A Nice Creck in your cakes in your cakes As cakes bake, a random crack can form on top as the batter rises in the oven. To ensure you end up with a nice, centred and even crack, score the top of the cake with a knife after it’s been baking for 10 minutes. Be sure to score it through the thin layer of film that has begun to form, then continue to bake the cake normally. The air in the cake will escape through the scored crack.

Easily whipped egg whites This is easier to do with eggs at room temperature. The eggs can also be kept for up to 4 days in a sealed container. Arm yourself with a large whisk. If the eggs are due to be cooked, it’s best to separate the egg whites from the yolks 2–3 days ahead of time and store them in the refrigerator in sealed bowls. Egg whites ‘broken’ by the cold will yield a smooth peak that won’t spread out during baking.

A perfect bake For evenly and thoroughly baked cakes, cook them for longer and at a lower temperature than indicated. For example, for a cake that is supposed to be baked for 40 minutes at 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4, try baking it at 160°C (325°F), Gas Mark 3, for 50–60 minutes. This way, the sides will be less dry and less cooked, and the middle will be baked to perfection.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Grate the zest from the orange and then squeeze out the juice. In a small saucepan, heat the orange juice with the sugar and the measured water. Add the zest (reserving some for decoration) and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the zest becomes translucent. Drain the zest.

Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Bring the cream to the boil in a saucepan, then pour it into a large bowl and add the chocolate. Stir briskly with a wooden spoon. Once the chocolate is completely melted, add the egg yolks one by one, stirring continuously until well combined.

Using an electric whisk, whip the egg whites to soft peaks with a pinch of salt. Fold them into the chocolate mixture, carefully scooping as you stir to avoid deflating the mousse. Add the orange zest. Pour the mousse into small ramekins and refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Decorate with the reserved orange zest before serving.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Mousse with Crystallized Orange Peel Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 1 unwaxed orange 120g caster sugar 125ml water 2 eggs 100ml single cream 180g dark chocolate, roughly grated A pinch of salt Grate the zest from the orange and then squeeze out the juice. In a small saucepan, heat the orange juice with the sugar and the measured water. Add the zest (reserving some for decoration) and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the zest becomes translucent. Drain the zest. Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Bring the cream to the boil in a saucepan, then pour it into a large bowl and add the chocolate. Stir briskly with a wooden spoon. Once the chocolate is completely melted, add the egg yolks one by one, stirring continuously until well combined. Using an electric whisk, whip the egg whites to soft peaks with a pinch of salt. Fold them into the chocolate mixture, carefully scooping as you stir to avoid deflating the mousse. Add the orange zest. Pour the mousse into small ramekins and refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Decorate with the reserved orange zest before serving.
recipes.title: Chocolate Mousse with Crystallized Orange Peel

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Slowly melt the chocolate with 100ml of the cream in a large bowl over a bain-marie. The water shouldn’t simmer or touch the bottom of the bowl.

Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature. In a bowl, whip the rest of the cold cream. Gradually fold the whipped cream into the white chocolate, carefully scooping the mixture with a rubber spatula.
Pour the mousse into small cups or into a serving dish. Refrigerate for 3 hours. Serving suggestion Enjoy this mousse with a red berry coulis.

recipes.searchText: White Chocolate Mousse Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 120g white chocolate, roughly chopped 400ml cold whipping cream Slowly melt the chocolate with 100ml of the cream in a large bowl over a bain-marie. The water shouldn’t simmer or touch the bottom of the bowl. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature. In a bowl, whip the rest of the cold cream. Gradually fold the whipped cream into the white chocolate, carefully scooping the mixture with a rubber spatula. Pour the mousse into small cups or into a serving dish. Refrigerate for 3 hours. Serving suggestion Enjoy this mousse with a red berry coulis.
recipes.title: White Chocolate Mousse

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200g dark chocolate, broken into small pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: The day before, separate the egg whites from the yolks. Melt the chocolate and butter over a bain-marie or in the microwave.
Remove the bowl from the bain-marie and mix the contents well. Allow it to cool, then whisk in the egg yolks briskly.
Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt, adding the icing sugar halfway through. Add to the chocolate mixture, carefully scooping the mixture with a rubber spatula as you stir.
Pour the mixture into ramekins or into a cake tin. Refrigerate the marquises for 12 hours before serving each decorated with a Cape gooseberry.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Marquise Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 3 eggs 200g dark chocolate, broken into small pieces 120g butter A pinch of salt 80g icing sugar 4–6 Cape gooseberries (physalis), to decorate The day before, separate the egg whites from the yolks. Melt the chocolate and butter over a bain-marie or in the microwave. Remove the bowl from the bain-marie and mix the contents well. Allow it to cool, then whisk in the egg yolks briskly. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt, adding the icing sugar halfway through. Add to the chocolate mixture, carefully scooping the mixture with a rubber spatula as you stir. Pour the mixture into ramekins or into a cake tin. Refrigerate the marquises for 12 hours before serving each decorated with a Cape gooseberry.
recipes.title: Chocolate Marquise

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a heavy-based saucepan, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until the mixture becomes frothy and light in colour. Add the cornflour, then the milk and cream while continuing to stir.
Place the saucepan over a low heat and stir the cream constantly until thickened, without letting it boil.

Remove from the heat and add the chocolate and vanilla extract. Mix well. Pour the cream into serving cups. Let them cool, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Serving suggestion Scatter shelled, chopped and lightly toasted pistachios on the top of each pudding.

recipes.searchText: Grandma’s Chocolate Pudding Crèmes & mousses Ingredients 6 egg yolks 150g caster sugar 1 level tablespoon cornflour 400ml milk 350ml single cream 125g dark chocolate, shaved or grated 1 teaspoon vanilla extract In a heavy-based saucepan, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until the mixture becomes frothy and light in colour. Add the cornflour, then the milk and cream while continuing to stir. Place the saucepan over a low heat and stir the cream constantly until thickened, without letting it boil. Remove from the heat and add the chocolate and vanilla extract. Mix well. Pour the cream into serving cups. Let them cool, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Serving suggestion Scatter shelled, chopped and lightly toasted pistachios on the top of each pudding.
recipes.title: Grandma’s Chocolate Pudding

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 small shop-bought meringues, broken into small pieces

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chocolate sauce
lines: 100g dark chocolate (70 per cent cocoa solids), roughly chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the chocolate sauce: place the chocolate in a bowl. Bring the cream to the boil in a saucepan, then immediately pour it over the chocolate. Cover for 5 minutes, then whisk well.

Prepare the chestnut cream: using a spatula, vigorously stir the chestnut cream to soften it. Whip the whipping cream into stiff peaks. Carefully fold it into the chestnut cream, without mixing too well, in order to achieve a marbled effect.
Scatter the meringue in the bottom of 4–6 small glasses, each with a volume of 120–150ml. Pour in the chocolate sauce, then top with the chestnut cream.

steps: Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks, gradually adding the sugar halfway through. Whisk the yolks with the mascarpone, then combine the mixtures carefully using a rubber spatula.

Dip the sponge fingers in the coffee and Marsala before arranging them across the bottom of individual cups or a large bowl. Cover them with the mascarpone mixture and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Dust the top with the cocoa powder just before serving.

Dip the sponge fingers in the coffee and Marsala before arranging them across the bottom of individual cups or a large bowl. Cover them with the mascarpone mixture and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Dust the top with the cocoa powder just before serving.
recipes.title: Tiramisú

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a large bowl, mix the cherries with 50g of the caster sugar and let them macerate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease a 24cm-long rectangular pie dish or an ovenproof porcelain cake tin.
Sift the flour into a large bowl, add the rest of the sugar and a pinch of salt. Break the eggs into the middle of the bowl and add the milk. Whisk well.
Distribute the cherries across the bottom of the pie dish, then pour in the mixture. Bake for 35–40 minutes.
Remove the clafoutis from the oven. Let it cool, then dust the top with icing sugar. Serve warm or cold in the baking tin.

recipes.searchText: Cherry Clafoutis Fruit desserts Ingredients 500g black cherries, pitted 100g caster sugar Butter for greasing 125g plain flour A pinch of salt 3 eggs 300ml milk Icing sugar In a large bowl, mix the cherries with 50g of the caster sugar and let them macerate for at least 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease a 24cm-long rectangular pie dish or an ovenproof porcelain cake tin. Sift the flour into a large bowl, add the rest of the sugar and a pinch of salt. Break the eggs into the middle of the bowl and add the milk. Whisk well. Distribute the cherries across the bottom of the pie dish, then pour in the mixture. Bake for 35–40 minutes. Remove the clafoutis from the oven. Let it cool, then dust the top with icing sugar. Serve warm or cold in the baking tin.

Fill the centre of each apple with chopped pistachios and 1 teaspoon of honey. Bake for 30 minutes. Halfway through cooking, baste the apples with the juices from the base of the dish and place a dollop of butter on top of each apple to make them caramelize.

lines: A scoop of vanilla ice cream or apricot sorbet, to serve (optional)

methodGroups.heading: Method

Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Cut the peaches and apricots into 5mm slices.

Serve the tian hot, with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or apricot sorbet, if using.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Cut a sheet of nonstick baking paper into 4 large rectangles. Divide the diced pineapple equally between the rectangles, then add to each the pulp of ½ a passion fruit, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, a pinch of cinnamon and 1 star anise.

Close the parcels tightly and bake for 20 minutes. Serve immediately. I’M BURSTING with fruit! Fruit is sovereign when it comes to dessert ingredients. Fruit takes centre stage in a wide range of recipes, from the simplest to the most sophisticated. It also makes it possible to end a meal on a light note. Once your fruit starts to become overripe, or if you have a large quantity of them, cooking them will allow you to enjoy them in the best possible way. A DELICIOUS every-day stir-fry Most fruit is delicious when fried, including apple and pear wedges, plums, apricots, peach halves, diced pineapple or mango slices. You can combine 1 pear, 1 apple and a handful of Mirabelle plums or 3–4 regular plums per person, for example. For these proportions, melt 50g butter in a nonstick frying pan and lightly brown the fruit over a medium heat. Dust the top with 2–3 tablespoons brown sugar until the juice has caramelized and coated the fruit. Serve with a scoop of ice cream or with whipped cream and biscuits. mixed berry coulis This is great for when you only have a handful of berries left. Blend them with some lemon juice and, if desired, some sugar, to make a delicious coulis. Pair it with fromage blanc (a soft, creamy cheese originating from the north of France). a classic apple dessert Baked apples are easy and inexpensive to make: core your apples and, if they’re not organic, peel them. Place them in a greased ovenproof dish, sprinkle with spices and dried fruit or nuts (cinnamon, ginger, allspice, cranberries, raisins, marzipan, walnuts, almonds or chopped hazelnuts) and top with a small piece of butter. Bake for about 40 minutes in an oven preheated to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. I’M BURSTING with fruit! Jams This is the best way to eat fruit all year round or to use fruit that is about to go bad. What’s more, jams go with almost anything! PECTIN IS YOUR FRIEND The success of your jam will depend on how much pectin your fruit contains. It acts as a natural gelatine and gives jam a nice, solid texture. Lemon juice helps to activate the pectin during cooking. Apples, citrus fruit and plums are particularly high in pectin. WHAT SHOULD THE FRUIT-TO-SUGAR RATIO BE? Traditionally, jam was made with equal parts fruit (peeled and stoned) and sugar. Nowadays, a lower ratio is preferable: a 60–70 per cent fruit-to-sugar ratio is enough, or 600–700g caster sugar for 1kg of fruit. Jam, marmalade or je y? A fruit preparation can only count as a preserve if it contains small pieces of fruit. Jam is made with crushed or strained fruit, not with whole fruit or fruit pieces. Marmalade is noted for its pieces of citrus fruit and peel in a transparent jelly. Lastly, jelly is made with fruit juice, separated from the pulp, extracted and carefully filtered. WHAT ABOUT FRUITS CONTAINING LITTLE PECTIN, LIKE STRAWBERRIES OR PEACHES? Cook the fruit over the course of two days so that it cooks through and loses much of its water. The first day, boil the fruit with the sugar for 15 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a bowl, allow it to cool and cover overnight. The following day, cook it again in a jam pan or heavy-based saucepan for about 30 minutes or until it passes the plate test (see here). BOTTLING Use glass jars with good quality lids. To sterilize them, boil them or place them in the oven with their covers for 10 minutes at 100°C (215°F), Gas Mark ¼. Fill them with boiling jam, carefully close them and place them upside down on a tea towel until completely cold. This will help create a vacuum effect and sterilize the opening, preserving the jam. THE PLATE TEST Place a plate in the refrigerator ahead of time until it’s cold. For the test, pour a drop of jam onto it and tip it. If the drop runs quickly down the plate, continue cooking it. If it remains in place as the plate tips, the jam is ready for bottling. RECOMMENDED PAIRINGS

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Split the ½ vanilla pod and scrape out the seeds. In a large nonstick frying pan, bring the measured water, sugar, lemon juice and vanilla pod and seeds to the boil, stirring constantly until the sugar has completely dissolved.
Add the plums and cook over a low heat for 10–15 minutes, regularly swirling the pan and basting the plums with their cooking juice.
Carefully drain the plums with a slotted spoon and place them in 1 large bowl or in 4 small serving cups. Cook the rest of the juice over a high heat for 2–3 minutes until thickened.
Pour the syrup on to the plums. Let them cool, then refrigerate before serving.

recipes.searchText: Pan-Fried Lemon Mirabelles Fruit desserts Ingredients ½ vanilla pod 50ml water 80g caster sugar 2 teaspoons freshly squeezed lemon juice 800g Mirabelle plums, halved and stoned Split the ½ vanilla pod and scrape out the seeds. In a large nonstick frying pan, bring the measured water, sugar, lemon juice and vanilla pod and seeds to the boil, stirring constantly until the sugar has completely dissolved. Add the plums and cook over a low heat for 10–15 minutes, regularly swirling the pan and basting the plums with their cooking juice. Carefully drain the plums with a slotted spoon and place them in 1 large bowl or in 4 small serving cups. Cook the rest of the juice over a high heat for 2–3 minutes until thickened. Pour the syrup on to the plums. Let them cool, then refrigerate before serving.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 large, very ripe bananas, peeled and halved lengthways

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Place the bananas in an oven dish just big enough to fit them and dust them with the cinnamon and nutmeg.
Mix the caster sugar with the citrus juices and stir until completely dissolved. Pour this syrup over the bananas. Bake for 20 minutes, regularly basting the bananas with their cooking juice.

At the end of the cooking time, there should be very little juice left in the dish. Remove the bananas from the oven and, if using, drizzle with some warm rum, set it on fire and allow it to flambé. Serve immediately, decorated with lime slices.

recipes.searchText: Roasted Spiced Bananas Fruit desserts Ingredients 4 large, very ripe bananas, peeled and halved lengthways ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon A pinch of ground nutmeg 4 tablespoons caster sugar 100ml freshly squeezed lime juice 150ml freshly squeezed orange juice 50ml dark rum (optional) Lime slices, to decorate Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Place the bananas in an oven dish just big enough to fit them and dust them with the cinnamon and nutmeg. Mix the caster sugar with the citrus juices and stir until completely dissolved. Pour this syrup over the bananas. Bake for 20 minutes, regularly basting the bananas with their cooking juice. At the end of the cooking time, there should be very little juice left in the dish. Remove the bananas from the oven and, if using, drizzle with some warm rum, set it on fire and allow it to flambé. Serve immediately, decorated with lime slices.
recipes.title: Roasted Spiced Bananas

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Arrange the figs in a greased ovenproof dish and, using a small knife, cut a deep criss-cross into the tops.
In a bowl, combine the chopped almonds, honey and cinnamon.
Pour the mixture over the figs and baste them with the butter and orange juice. Bake for 10 minutes. Serve hot.

recipes.searchText: Roasted Figs with Almonds Fruit desserts Ingredients 12 figs 30g almonds, roughly chopped 4 tablespoons honey A pinch of ground cinnamon 20g melted butter Juice of ½ an orange Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Arrange the figs in a greased ovenproof dish and, using a small knife, cut a deep criss-cross into the tops. In a bowl, combine the chopped almonds, honey and cinnamon. Pour the mixture over the figs and baste them with the butter and orange juice. Bake for 10 minutes. Serve hot.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 small piece of ginger, peeled and grated

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Cover an oven tray with nonstick baking paper. Place 2 filo dough sheets on top of each other, brush them with a little of the melted butter and sprinkle some icing sugar on top. Cut out six 12cm discs and place them on the oven tray. Bake for 3–5 minutes, until golden. Repeat with the other 6 sheets.
Split the vanilla pod in half lengthways and scrape out the seeds. Place the pineapple in a large bowl. Add the ginger, ground cardamom seeds, brown sugar, vanilla pod and seeds. Mix well.
In a frying pan, add the rest of the melted butter and the pineapple. Cook over a medium heat for about 10 minutes, stirring often. Remove the vanilla and cardamom pods.

Assemble the millefeuilles: place 2 filo pastry discs on each serving dish. Scatter with pineapple cubes and pistachios, then cover with 2 further pastry discs, and so on, finishing with 2 pastry discs on top – you should have 8 pastry discs in each stack. Serve drizzled with mixed berry coulis, if using. Serving suggestion Decorate with icing sugar, pistachios and a small bunch of redcurrants.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Plunge the peaches in a saucepan of boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain and let them cool a little.
Peel, halve and stone the peaches. Cut 4 of the peaches into cubes and the other 2 into quarters.
In a frying pan, melt 50g of the butter over a medium heat. Once it begins to froth, add the orange zest, then sprinkle the sugar all over and allow it to caramelize lightly.
Add the peaches and soften them for 1–2 minutes, turning them once carefully to coat them in caramel.
Carefully remove the fruit using a slotted spoon and set the peach pieces aside.
Pour the orange and lemon juices into the frying pan and reduce over a high heat until syrupy.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Melt the rest of the butter and brush the brick pastry sheets with it.
Place a quarter of the cubed peaches in the centre of each brick pastry sheet.
Fold into parcels and secure each one with a cocktail stick.
Place the parcels carefully on a nonstick baking tray and bake for 6–8 minutes, until golden.
Pour the orange caramel on to warm serving dishes, place a peach parcel on each one and surround it with the caramelized peach quarters. Decorate with mint leaves before serving.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 6 apples (preferably boskoop), peeled, cored and diced
1 ripe mango, peeled, stoned and diced
Zest of ½ unwaxed lemon or lime

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Split the vanilla pods in half lengthways and scrape out the seeds.
Combine the apples, mango, brown sugar and vanilla seeds and pods in a saucepan. Place over a low heat and mix well. Cook gently for 20–30 minutes, until the fruit is well done and easily crushed.

At the end of the cooking time, remove the vanilla pods from the mixture. Crush the fruit with a fork or blend it for a smoother texture. Allow it to cool and sprinkle lemon or lime zest on top before serving.

Combine the apples, mango, brown sugar and vanilla seeds and pods in a saucepan. Place over a low heat and mix well. Cook gently for 20–30 minutes, until the fruit is well done and easily crushed. At the end of the cooking time, remove the vanilla pods from the mixture. Crush the fruit with a fork or blend it for a smoother texture. Allow it to cool and sprinkle lemon or lime zest on top before serving.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 20 small shop-bought meringues, broken into pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blend a quarter of the fruit with the icing sugar and lemon juice. If the coulis contains seeds, pass it through a small strainer.
Fill 6 small cups or glasses by alternating the meringue pieces, cream, the remaining fruit and the coulis. Do not stir the cream to mix it through. Serve cold.

recipes.searchText: Eton Mess Fruit desserts Ingredients 500g fresh mixed berries 1½ tablespoons icing sugar 2 tablespoons lemon juice 20 small shop-bought meringues, broken into pieces 400ml crème fraîche Blend a quarter of the fruit with the icing sugar and lemon juice. If the coulis contains seeds, pass it through a small strainer. Fill 6 small cups or glasses by alternating the meringue pieces, cream, the remaining fruit and the coulis. ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 Williams pears, not too ripe, peeled, with the stem retained

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Use a peeler to remove the rind from the lemon, then squeeze out the juice. Split the vanilla pod in half lengthways.
Pour the pear juice into a saucepan and reduce it over a low heat for 15 minutes. Add the wine, spices and lemon rind, then bring to a simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, douse the pears in the lemon juice. Add them to the syrup and cook them over a low heat for 15 minutes, turning them regularly. Serve them warm with a little of the syrup.

recipes.searchText: Pears Poached in Sweet Wine Fruit desserts Ingredients 1 unwaxed lemon 1 vanilla pod 500ml pear juice 500ml sweet white wine 2 cardamom pods 1 cinnamon stick 2 star anise 4 Williams pears, not too ripe, peeled, with the stem retained Use a peeler to remove the rind from the lemon, then squeeze out the juice. Split the vanilla pod in half lengthways. Pour the pear juice into a saucepan and reduce it over a low heat for 15 minutes. Add the wine, spices and lemon rind, then bring to a simmer for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, douse the pears in the lemon juice. Add them to the syrup and cook them over a low heat for 15 minutes, turning them regularly. Serve them warm with a little of the syrup.
recipes.title: Pears Poached in Sweet Wine

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the pineapple: remove the skin and the ‘eyes’ with the tip of a sharp knife. Cut into very thin slices, ideally using a mandolin. Lay the slices on a large dish, taking care not to overlap them.

Prepare the syrup: place the caster sugar and the measured water in a heavy-based saucepan. Split the vanilla pod in half lengthways and scrape the seeds into the saucepan, using the tip of a small knife. Bring the syrup to a slow boil, swirling the saucepan to distribute the heat evenly until large bubbles start to form.

Drizzle the hot syrup on to the pineapple slices, cover with clingfilm and refrigerate for 1 hour. Serve cold. PASTRY-MAKING challenges and sol tions! My crème anglaise is l mpy When you pour your hot egg–sugar–milk mixture into the saucepan to be cooked, you should be able to see a fine layer of mousse on top. Then comes a fleeting moment in which this mousse suddenly retracts toward the edges of the saucepan. That’s the precise moment when you should stop the cooking by pouring the cream into a large cold bowl. After this stage, the cream will curdle, as the temperature will be higher than 83°C. If your crème anglaise is still lumpy, blend it for a few seconds with a hand blender. Out of sight, out of mind! An unpleasant film ON TOP OF my creams To prevent a film from forming on your crème anglaise or crème pâtissière as it cools, cover it in clingfilm, placing the clingfilm directly on the surface. This way, you’ll also avoid ending up with a lumpy cream. My macaron shells are covered in bubbles A good macaronage is the key to making successful macarons. Macaronage is the process of adding whipped egg whites to the almond–sugar mixture. Unlike the method used when making cake batter, they should be incorporated vigorously. Don’t be afraid to mix them in well, or until the batter forms a ribbon when you lift the spatula. Macaron batter should be more ‘fluid’ than you might think. Here’s another trick for smoothing out the surface of your macaron shells: blend the icing sugar and ground almonds together, then sift everything into a fine powder. My cake caves in like a so fflé It had risen nicely, it was pretty and then it went and caved in like a soufflé as it cooled. The problem? Too much baking powder. Try to reduce the quantity by, for example, adding 2 teaspoons instead of a whole sachet. My pastry dough IS ALWAYS TOO soft Forget about ceramic or glass pie dishes. Pastry dough will never cook correctly in these types of dishes. Opt instead for classic metal tins, which can be lightly greased before use and won’t need to be greased again later. There’s a reason why professionals only use these! At a pinch, use a nonstick baking tin.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Using a small, sharp knife, peel the grapefruit and oranges, removing any pith. Slide the blade between each membrane and carefully remove the citrus pieces. Place these in a large bowl with the mint, ginger and agave syrup, then squeeze out any remaining juice and add it to the bowl.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Add the passion fruit pulp and serve cold.

recipes.searchText: Citrus and Mint Nage Fruit desserts Ingredients 3 grapefruit 3 oranges 10–15 mint leaves, finely chopped ¼ teaspoon grated ginger 2 tablespoons agave syrup 1–2 passion fruit Using a small, sharp knife, peel the grapefruit and oranges, removing any pith. Slide the blade between each membrane and carefully remove the citrus pieces. Place these in a large bowl with the mint, ginger and agave syrup, then squeeze out any remaining juice and add it to the bowl. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Add the passion fruit pulp and serve cold.
recipes.title: Citrus and Mint Nage

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: The day before, cook the rhubarb, caster sugar and star anise in the measured water for 15 minutes. Drain the rhubarb, allow it to cool and return it to the syrup. Allow it to rest overnight.

The next day, make the Chantilly cream. Split the vanilla pod in half lengthways, scrape out the seeds and mix them into the cream. Whip the cream, slowly at first, then on high speed. Once it has doubled in volume, add the icing sugar.
Pour the rhubarb and syrup into 4 bowls. Serve the Chantilly cream on the side.

recipes.searchText: Poached Rhubarb with Vanilla Chantilly Cream Fruit desserts Ingredients For the chantilly cream 400g rhubarb, cut into 2.5cm pieces 120g caster sugar 2 star anise 750ml boiling water 1 vanilla pod 250ml very cold whipping cream 20g icing sugar The day before, cook the rhubarb, caster sugar and star anise in the measured water for 15 minutes. Drain the rhubarb, allow it to cool and return it to the syrup. Allow it to rest overnight. The next day, make the Chantilly cream. Split the vanilla pod in half lengthways, scrape out the seeds and mix them into the cream. Whip the cream, slowly at first, then on high speed. Once it has doubled in volume, add the icing sugar. Pour the rhubarb and syrup into 4 bowls. Serve the Chantilly cream on the side.
recipes.title: Poached Rhubarb with Vanilla Chantilly Cream

ingredientGroups.heading: For the watermelon coulis
lines: ¼ watermelon (about 800g), rind removed, deseeded and diced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the watermelon coulis: refrigerate one-third of the watermelon in a small bowl. Blend the rest with the lemon juice until you obtain a smooth and watery coulis.

Prepare the basil syrup: in a small saucepan, slowly heat the measured water and caster sugar, stirring until the sugar has completely dissolved. Bring to the boil, remove from the heat and add the chopped basil. Cover and let it stand for 10 minutes, then strain. Mix the watermelon coulis with the basil syrup and refrigerate for 2 hours.

At the last minute, pour the mixture into 4 serving bowls and top with the reserved watermelon. Decorate each portion with basil leaves and serve cold. Serving suggestion If it’s very hot out, add a few ice cubes to the bowls.

recipes.searchText: Watermelon and Basil Soup Fruit desserts For the watermelon coulis For the basil syrup For the decoration ¼ watermelon (about 800g), rind removed, deseeded and diced 2 tablespoons lemon juice 150ml water 40g caster sugar 1 tablespoon finely chopped basil A few basil leaves Prepare the watermelon coulis: refrigerate one-third of the watermelon in a small bowl. Blend the rest with the lemon juice until you obtain a smooth and watery coulis. Prepare the basil syrup: in a small saucepan, slowly heat the measured water and caster sugar, stirring until the sugar has completely dissolved. Bring to the boil, remove from the heat and add the chopped basil. Cover and let it stand for 10 minutes, then strain. Mix the watermelon coulis with the basil syrup and refrigerate for 2 hours. At the last minute, pour the mixture into 4 serving bowls and top with the reserved watermelon. Decorate each portion with basil leaves and serve cold. Serving suggestion If it’s very hot out, add a few ice cubes to the bowls.
recipes.title: Watermelon and Basil Soup

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the honey and star anise in a frying pan until the honey becomes frothy. Add the cherries and cook for another 5 minutes while stirring continuously.

Deglaze the pan with 1–2 tablespoons water. Place the cherries in small bowls and sprinkle pistachios on top. Serve hot or warm. Serving suggestion Serve the cherries with a few spoonfuls of fromage blanc (a soft, creamy cheese from the north of France) or soft sheep cheese.

recipes.searchText: Pan-Fried Cherries with Honey and Pistachios Fruit desserts Ingredients 1 tablespoon honey 2 star anise 400g cherries, pitted 2 tablespoons roughly chopped pistachios Heat the honey and star anise in a frying pan until the honey becomes frothy. Add the cherries and cook for another 5 minutes while stirring continuously. Deglaze the pan with 1–2 tablespoons water. Place the cherries in small bowls and sprinkle pistachios on top. Serve hot or warm. Serving suggestion Serve the cherries with a few spoonfuls of fromage blanc (a soft, creamy cheese from the north of France) or soft sheep cheese.
recipes.title: Pan-Fried Cherries with Honey and Pistachios

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300g raspberries + a few extra, to decorate
500g fresh lychees, shelled and pitted (or 260g drained lychees from a tin)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Purée the raspberries in a blender. Pour the raspberry purée into a saucepan with the lemon juice and caster sugar. Bring to the boil and cook for about 3 minutes.
Pour the mixture into 4 bowls and allow to cool to room temperature before refrigerating. Serve cold with the lychees and extra raspberries arranged on top.

recipes.searchText: Chilled Lychees and Raspberries Fruit desserts Ingredients 300g raspberries + a few extra, to decorate 2 tablespoons lemon juice 70g caster sugar 500g fresh lychees, shelled and pitted (or 260g drained lychees from a tin) Purée the raspberries in a blender. Pour the raspberry purée into a saucepan with the lemon juice and caster sugar. Bring to the boil and cook for about 3 minutes. Pour the mixture into 4 bowls and allow to cool to room temperature before refrigerating. Serve cold with the lychees and extra raspberries arranged on top.
recipes.title: Chilled Lychees and Raspberries

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150g fresh or frozen blackcurrants + extra for decorating

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Dilute the blackcurrant cordial in half a glass of water. Soak the sponge fingers in the blackcurrant juice, then use some of them to line the bottom and sides of an 18cm Charlotte tin.

Add a layer of blackcurrant sorbet, scatter with some blackcurrants and cover with another layer of soaked sponge fingers. Repeat until all the ingredients have been used up. Freeze for at least 2 hours.

Meanwhile, prepare the crème anglaise: split the vanilla pod in half lengthways. In a small saucepan, bring the milk and vanilla pod to the boil. Remove from the heat and let it stand for 20 minutes. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Remove the vanilla pod from the milk and scrape out its seeds. Bring the milk and vanilla seeds to the boil. Pour the boiling milk on to the egg yolk mixture while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon. Return the mixture to the saucepan over a low heat while turning the pan until the cream coats the back of a spoon. Place the saucepan in a large bowl filled with ice water (or pour the cream into a chilled bowl or jug), to stop the cooking. Refrigerate.
Remove the Charlotte from its tin just before serving. Decorate with the extra blackcurrants and the mint sprig and serve with the crème anglaise on the side.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 × 22cm sponge cake, preferably homemade (see here, with the zest of 1 unwaxed lemon added to the dough), sliced horizontally into 3 layers

ingredientGroups.heading: For the apples
lines: 4 apples (preferably boskoop), peeled, deseeded and diced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the apples: cook them in a saucepan over a low heat for 10 minutes with the sugar, lemon zest, wine and measured water. The fruit should be cooked through and the liquid should have evaporated. Mash the apples with a fork. Add the crumbled amaretti biscuits.

Prepare the filling: whip the cream. In a small saucepan, whisk the egg yolks and sugar until pale in colour, then place them over a bain-marie. Whisk them for a few moments, then remove them from the heat and keep whisking them until they’re cool. Carefully fold in the whipped cream.
Mix the cream with the apples and amaretti biscuits.

Cut out a sheet of nonstick baking paper the same size as the sponge cake. Place the first layer of cake on to the paper. Use a spatula to spread half the cream mixture on top. Add the next layer of cake and repeat, then cover with the last layer.
Freeze the cake for 30 minutes, then refrigerate until ready to eat. Dust with icing sugar just before serving.

Add the next layer of cake and repeat, then cover with the last layer. Freeze the cake for 30 minutes, then refrigerate until ready to eat. Dust with icing sugar just before serving.
recipes.title: Apple and Almond Semifreddo

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: The day before, hull the strawberries and dice into small pieces. In a large bowl, mix the strawberries with the caster sugar.
Prepare the syrup: in a small saucepan, bring the water and sugar to the boil.

In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks while gradually adding the boiling syrup. Remove from the heat and continue to whisk the mixture until completely cold and frothy. Use a spatula to carefully add the strawberries and their juice.
Whip the cream and carefully fold it into the mixture.
Line the sides of a soufflé tin with nonstick baking paper. Pour the mixture into the soufflé tin and freeze for at least 12 hours.
Before serving, remove the surrounding baking paper and dust the top of the soufflé with cocoa powder, if using.

recipes.searchText: Frozen Strawberry Soufflé Frozen desserts Ingredients For the syrup 250g strawberries 30g caster sugar 6 egg yolks 250g very cold whipping cream 1 tablespoon cocoa powder (optional) 200ml water 70g caster sugar The day before, hull the strawberries and dice into small pieces. In a large bowl, mix the strawberries with the caster sugar. Prepare the syrup: in a small saucepan, bring the water and sugar to the boil. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks while gradually adding the boiling syrup. Remove from the heat and continue to whisk the mixture until completely cold and frothy. Use a spatula to carefully add the strawberries and their juice. Whip the cream and carefully fold it into the mixture. Line the sides of a soufflé tin with nonstick baking paper. Pour the mixture into the soufflé tin and freeze for at least 12 hours. Before serving, remove the surrounding baking paper and dust the top of the soufflé with cocoa powder, if using.
recipes.title: Frozen Strawberry Soufflé

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: The night before, prepare the chestnut ice cream: bring the milk and cream to the boil. Split the vanilla pod in half lengthways, scrape out the seeds and add both the vanilla pod and seeds to the saucepan. Let it infuse for 30 minutes, then strain.
In a separate saucepan, whisk the egg yolks with the caster sugar. Add the vanilla milk and cook over a low heat until the mixture thickens (it should never come to the boil).
Add the chestnut cream and purée. Let it cool and refrigerate for 3 hours. Churn it in an ice cream maker, then pour it into a springform tin and freeze it.
Prepare the dough: sift the ground almonds and icing sugar into a large bowl.
Whip the egg whites into soft peaks with a little of the caster sugar. Once they’ve puffed up, add the rest of the sugar all at once. Stir for 1 minute.
Using a spatula, fold the almond mixture into the egg whites. Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F), Gas Mark 3.

Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper and draw two 20cm circles on to the paper. Fill a 1.5cm piping bag with the egg white mixture and pipe it into the traced circles, drawing a spiral from the outside in.
Bake for 30 minutes, then immediately reduce the oven temperature to 140°C (275°F), Gas Mark 1, and bake for another hour. Let the meringue discs cool completely before removing them from the tray.
The following day, place a meringue disc on a serving plate. Spread the chestnut ice cream on top of the disc.
Place the other disc on top of the ice cream.
Dust icing sugar on top and decorate with marrons glacés, if using.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500g fresh or frozen blackcurrants, stalks removed

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Place the cottage cheese in a colander lined with 2 sheets of kitchen paper and drain for 1 hour.
Place the blackcurrants in a blender and mix, then strain the resulting coulis with a strainer.
Drizzle the lemon juice over the diced pears.

In a small saucepan, heat the sugar and measured water on a low heat, stirring until the sugar has completely dissolved. Bring to the boil, then remove from the heat at the first sign of bubbles. Add two-thirds of the coulis and mix.
Vigorously whisk the drained cottage cheese with the mascarpone, then add them to the blackcurrant syrup and mix well. Pour half the mixture into a 18–20cm round cake tin and freeze for 30 minutes.
Once the mixture has set sufficiently, cover it with the diced pears, then pour the rest of the blackcurrant cream on top of the pears and freeze again for at least 3 hours.

Remove the dessert from the mould and wait 15 minutes before cutting into it. Serve with the remaining coulis. Serving suggestion Decorate this dessert with some biscuits, fruit pieces and mixed berries.

recipes.searchText: Pear and Blackcurrant Frozen Delight Frozen desserts Ingredients 350g very cold cottage cheese 500g fresh or frozen blackcurrants, stalks removed Juice of 1 lemon 2 pears, peeled, cored and diced 130g caster sugar 100ml water 150g very cold mascarpone Place the cottage cheese in a colander lined with 2 sheets of kitchen paper and drain for 1 hour. Place the blackcurrants in a blender and mix, then strain the resulting coulis with a strainer. Drizzle the lemon juice over the diced pears. In a small saucepan, heat the sugar and measured water on a low heat, stirring until the sugar has completely dissolved. Bring to the boil, then remove from the heat at the first sign of bubbles. Add two-thirds of the coulis and mix. Vigorously whisk the drained cottage cheese with the mascarpone, then add them to the blackcurrant syrup and mix well. Pour half the mixture into a 18–20cm round cake tin and freeze for 30 minutes. Once the mixture has set sufficiently, cover it with the diced pears, then pour the rest of the blackcurrant cream on top of the pears and freeze again for at least 3 hours. Remove the dessert from the mould and wait 15 minutes before cutting into it. Serve with the remaining coulis. Serving suggestion Decorate this dessert with some biscuits, fruit pieces and mixed berries.

ingredientGroups.heading: For the filling
lines: Vanilla ice cream (or other flavour of your choice)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the choux pastry: pour the measured water and milk into a saucepan with the salt, sugar and butter. Bring to the boil while stirring. Add the flour all at once. Stir vigorously with a spatula until the batter becomes smooth and even. Continue to stir for 2–3 minutes after it starts to detach from the sides and bottom of the saucepan, in order to thicken it. Remove from the heat and let it cool. Add the eggs one at a time while continuing to stir the mixture. Use a spatula to regularly lift the mixture as you stir. Once it falls off the spatula in ribbons, it’s ready.

Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Place the pastry in a piping bag with a smooth nozzle and pipe 30 walnut-sized dough balls onto the baking tray. Bake for 7 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 170°C (340°F), Gas Mark 3, and bake for another 15 minutes. To ensure the pastry is cooked through, gently press down on a choux bun with your finger. It shouldn’t give. If it does, continue to bake.
Prepare the chocolate sauce: bring the cream to the boil, pour it over the chocolate and mix well.

Cut off the top of each choux bun. Fill the choux buns with vanilla ice cream and cover with the tops. Place the profiteroles in a serving dish or in individual serving bowls. Top them with the warm chocolate sauce. Serve immediately.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 60g crushed nuts: almonds, walnuts, pistachios, and so on, mixed or just 1 type
1 litre ice cream of your choice (chocolate, vanilla, strawberry)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Toast the almonds (not the walnuts or pistachios) for about 5 minutes in a dry frying pan, stirring continuously. Take the ice cream out of the freezer.

In a small saucepan, bring the measured water and caster sugar to the boil. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks while gradually adding the boiling syrup. Whisk the mixture until it’s completely cooled and frothy. Whip the cream and carefully fold it into the mixture. Add the nuts and candied fruit.
Using a spatula, spread the ice cream along the sides and bottom of an 18cm Charlotte tin. Pour in the prepared mixture and freeze for 4 hours.
Before serving the cassata, run the tin under hot water for a few seconds, then flip the dessert on to a serving dish.

The basic ingredients are the same: a fruit coulis or purée and syrup for sorbets, and a crème anglaise base for ice creams. Place your mixture in a covered container in the freezer, stir it a few times at the start of the freezing process, cut it into pieces and zap it in a blender. Nice cream piña colada Serves 4 Preparation time: 5 minutes 600g frozen, diced pineapple + 1 slice of fresh pineapple, diced 200ml coconut milk 100ml white rum (optional) 2 tablespoons brown sugar Zest of 1 unwaxed lime 1 Place all the ingredients except for the fresh pineapple and lime zest in a blender. Start by pulsing them, then blend continuously until the texture is creamy. Serve the nice cream immediately, sprucing it up with the fresh, diced pineapple and lime zest, or freeze it in a freezer tray – in which case you should remove it from the freezer 10 minutes before serving. A ‘nice cream’ is a quick and easy ice cream made without a centrifuge or ice cream maker. Instead, it’s made with frozen fruit placed directly in a blender. You often find them made from very ripe bananas, as these make them creamy, but any fruit will do. The result is a very versatile ice cream with a texture similar to ‘Italian’ ice cream. It’s best when served immediately. Man o–lime sorbet Serves 4 Preparation time: 10 minutes Cooking time: 5 minutes Resting time: 3 hours 150ml water 1 unwaxed lime 60g caster sugar 2 ripe mangoes + ½ to serve 1 Prepare a syrup with the measured water, the zest and juice of the lime and the sugar. Bring it to the boil for 5 minutes, then allow it to cool. 2 Blend the mango pulp with the warm syrup, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours. 3 Place the mixture in an ice cream maker or centrifuge. Pour the ice cream into a freezer tray and freeze for about 1 hour so that it hardens again. Serve with fresh mango slices. Mixed berry ranita Serves 4 Preparation time: 10 minutes Freezing time: 3 hours and 20 minutes 30g caster sugar A little lemon juice 250g mixed berries (or 200ml mixed berry coulis) 100ml water 1 Prepare a syrup by combining the sugar, lemon juice and fruit with the measured water. Pour it into a metal bowl and place it in the freezer. 2 After 20 minutes, scrape the surface with a fork and return it to the freezer. Repeat this operation 2 or 3 times until the whole sorbet is in flakes. Expect this to take about 3 hours in total. Serve immediately in order to preserve the correct texture. Party granitas! • Leave out the lemon juice and substitute the water with 100ml Champagne. • Serve the granita in glasses topped with mixed berry skewers. • For a presentation worthy of a good cocktail party, decorate the glasses by dipping the rims in lemon juice and sugar. Fruit popsi es Preparation time: 10 minutes Freezing time: 3 hours Mango: 2 very ripe mangoes A little lemon juice 1 teaspoon caster sugar Strawberry: 250g strawberries A little lemon juice Lemon: Syrup made with 4 tablespoons lemon juice, 150g caster sugar and 300ml water Blend your chosen ingredients to obtain a smooth coulis. To make lemon popsicles, prepare the syrup beforehand and allow it to cool. Slip in a few pieces of fruit, then place the mixture in popsicle moulds. Freeze for 3 hours.
recipes.title: Frozen Chocolate Parfait with Caramelized Almonds

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the raspberry purée: crush the raspberries in a blender to make a purée.
Plunge the peaches in boiling water for 30 seconds, immediately run them under cold water, then peel them.

Prepare the syrup: split the vanilla pod in half lengthways and scrape out the seeds. Bring the measured water, caster sugar and vanilla pod and seeds to the boil for 5 minutes. Plunge the peaches into the syrup and cook over a low heat for 7–8 minutes, turning them often. Drain the peaches and let them cool completely, then halve and stone them.

Cut the peaches into wedges and divide them between 4 dessert glasses. Drizzle with the raspberry purée and top with scoops of vanilla ice cream. Serving suggestion You can also serve this with some Chantilly cream and flaked almonds.

recipes.title: Peach Melba

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 6 Williams pears, peeled, with the stalk left on

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the syrup: bring the measured water and sugar to the boil.
Prepare the pears: cook the pears in the syrup for 20–30 minutes. Once softened, drain and refrigerate them.
Bring the 60ml of measured water to the boil. Place the chocolate in a saucepan and pour the boiling water on top, mixing well until the chocolate has melted. Add the cream.
Place a pear in each serving dish and cover in hot chocolate sauce, then serve a scoop of vanilla ice cream alongside.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Cut the tops off 8 of the mandarins with a bread knife, then scoop out the pulp with a sharp-edged spoon, taking care not to pierce the rind. Freeze the hollowed-out mandarins and their tops.
Strain the pulp through a sieve, pressing down on it with a spatula. Squeeze the remaining mandarins to obtain 800ml juice.
Dissolve the sugar in the measured water. Add the syrup to the juice and place in a plastic container. Freeze for at least 3 hours.

About 30 minutes before serving, whip the egg white with a fork. Using a large knife, dice the sorbet into small cubes. Blitz the cubes in a food processor, gradually adding two-thirds of the egg white. Stop when you’ve obtained a pale and frothy sorbet. Scoop the sorbet into the hollowed out mandarins. Replace the mandarin tops and freeze for 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.searchText: Mandarin Sorbet Frozen desserts Ingredients 16 mandarins 80g caster sugar 80ml hot water 1 egg white Cut the tops off 8 of the mandarins with a bread knife, then scoop out the pulp with a sharp-edged spoon, taking care not to pierce the rind. Freeze the hollowed-out mandarins and their tops. Strain the pulp through a sieve, pressing down on it with a spatula. Squeeze the remaining mandarins to obtain 800ml juice. Dissolve the sugar in the measured water. Add the syrup to the juice and place in a plastic container. Freeze for at least 3 hours. About 30 minutes before serving, whip the egg white with a fork. Using a large knife, dice the sorbet into small cubes. Blitz the cubes in a food processor, gradually adding two-thirds of the egg white. Stop when you’ve obtained a pale and frothy sorbet. Scoop the sorbet into the hollowed out mandarins. Replace the mandarin tops and freeze for 30 minutes before serving.
recipes.title: Mandarin Sorbet

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Let the vanilla ice cream soften slightly before scooping it into a loaf tin. Place it back in the freezer until just before needed. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6.
Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Prepare the batter: sift the flour into a bowl. Melt the butter in a saucepan and allow it to cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine the eggs and caster sugar. Place over a simmering bain-marie and begin to whisk. Continue to stir until the mixture has thickened.

Remove the bowl from the bain-marie and use an electric handheld mixer to whisk the mixture until completely cooled. Place 2 tablespoons of this mixture in a small bowl and add the butter. Gradually sprinkle the sifted flour into the mixing bowl, then combine with the contents of the small bowl.

Pour the sponge batter into the lined baking tray and bake for 15 minutes. Use the knife test to ensure the cake is fully cooked by inserting the blade, which should come out clean. Let the cake cool.
Cut out 2 rectangles of sponge the same size as the loaf tin. Increase the oven temperature to 250°C (485°F), Gas Mark 9.
Prepare the meringue: whip the egg whites into soft peaks, adding half the sugar. Once doubled in volume, pour in the rest of the sugar and the vanilla extract.
Prepare the syrup: bring the sugar and measured water to the boil. Let it cool, then add half the liqueur. Place 1 sponge rectangle on an ovenproof plate. Use a brush to soak it in syrup.
Just before serving, turn on the grill. Scoop the vanilla ice cream on to the sponge and cover it with the other sponge rectangle. Use a spatula to spread half the meringue on top until smooth.

Fill a piping bag with a starshaped nozzle with the rest of the meringue and use this to decorate the top of the dessert. Dust the top with icing sugar and place the dessert under the grill for 3 minutes with the door open.
Heat the rest of the liqueur in a small saucepan. Set it on fire and pour it over the dessert. Allow it to flambé in front of your guests and serve immediately.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1.2kg very ripe mangoes, peeled, stoned and diced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Place the mangoes in a blender or food mill and purée: this should yield 800g of purée. Juice the lemon or lime.
Melt the sugar in the measured water.

Whisk the mango purée with the lemon or lime juice. Add sugar syrup to taste (some mangoes are so naturally sweet that no sugar will be needed). Refrigerate for at least 3 hours before churning it in an ice cream maker.

recipes.searchText: Mango Sorbet Frozen desserts Ingredients 1.2kg very ripe mangoes, peeled, stoned and diced 1 lemon or lime 50g caster sugar 100ml hot water Place the mangoes in a blender or food mill and purée: this should yield 800g of purée. methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a saucepan, bring the milk and cream to the boil. Remove from the heat, add the chopped mint and let it stand for 20 minutes, covered. Strain.

In another saucepan, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar. Pour the infused milk into the saucepan and cook over a low heat (without bringing it to the boil), stirring with a wooden spoon until thickened (the mixture should reach 83°C/181°F).
Immediately pour the cream into a large bowl placed over ice in order to halt the cooking. Let it cool, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours before churning it in an ice cream maker.

If you don’t have an ice cream maker, put the mixture in the freezer, mix it in a food processor after 2 hours, then put it back in the freezer for another 2 hours. Serve in individual dessert bowls, decorated with fresh mint leaves.

recipes.searchText: Mint Ice Cream Frozen desserts Ingredients 500ml whole milk 250ml whipping cream 250g fresh mint leaves, chopped 6 egg yolks 140g caster sugar Fresh mint leaves, to decorate In a saucepan, bring the milk and cream to the boil. Remove from the heat, add the chopped mint and let it stand for 20 minutes, covered. Strain. In another saucepan, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar. Pour the infused milk into the saucepan and cook over a low heat (without bringing it to the boil), stirring with a wooden spoon until thickened (the mixture should reach 83°C/181°F). Immediately pour the cream into a large bowl placed over ice in order to halt the cooking. Let it cool, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours before churning it in an ice cream maker.
