Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Generously grease the cups of a canelé tray. Melt the butter. Combine the eggs and egg yolks with the icing sugar and whisk until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the melted butter and the rum. Incorporate the flour and then thin out the mixture with the vanilla-infused milk. Fill the cups of the canelé tray three-quarters full. Bake for 45 minutes. Remove the canelés from the tray as soon as they’re out of the oven. Serve cold.
recipes.title: Canelés

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Sift the flour. Melt the butter slowly over a bain-marie or in the microwave. Combine the sugar and ground almonds. Add the flour, then gradually fold in 3 of the egg whites and mix well. Add the melted butter when it’s barely warm. In a separate bowl, whip the last egg white into soft peaks and carefully fold it into the mixture.
Grease some small barquette or oval baking moulds. Pour the mixture into the moulds, filling each two-thirds full. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F), Gas Mark 7. Bake the visitandine cakes for 8–10 minutes. They should be golden on the outside and moist on the inside. Remove them from their tins while still warm.

recipes.searchText: Visitandine Cakes Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 40g plain flour 185g butter + extra for greasing 125g caster sugar 125g ground almonds 4 egg whites Sift the flour. Melt the butter slowly over a bain-marie or in the microwave. Combine the sugar and ground almonds. Add the flour, then gradually fold in 3 of the egg whites and mix well. Add the melted butter when it’s barely warm. In a separate bowl, whip the last egg white into soft peaks and carefully fold it into the mixture. Grease some small barquette or oval baking moulds. Pour the mixture into the moulds, filling each two-thirds full. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F), Gas Mark 7. Bake the visitandine cakes for 8–10 minutes. They should be golden on the outside and moist on the inside. Remove them from their tins while still warm.
recipes.title: Visitandine Cakes

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper.
In a large bowl, combine the butter and sugars and mix well with a wooden spoon. Add the eggs, one at a time. Sift the flour, pour it into the mixture all at once and mix well.
Place the batter in a piping bag with a 6mm piping nozzle and pipe 5cm strips of batter onto the nonstick paper, leaving a gap of 2cm between each strip.
The langues de chats won’t fit on a single baking tray. Bake each batch for 4–5 minutes. Once the biscuits have cooled, keep them in a sealed container.

recipes.searchText: Langue De Chat Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 125g butter, at room temperature 7.5g (1 heaped teaspoon) vanilla sugar 75–100g caster sugar, according to taste 2 eggs 125g plain flour Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. In a large bowl, combine the butter and sugars and mix well with a wooden spoon. Add the eggs, one at a time. Sift the flour, pour it into the mixture all at once and mix well. Place the batter in a piping bag with a 6mm piping nozzle and pipe 5cm strips of batter onto the nonstick paper, leaving a gap of 2cm between each strip. The langues de chats won’t fit on a single baking tray. Bake each batch for 4–5 minutes. Once the biscuits have cooled, keep them in a sealed container.
recipes.title: Langue De Chat Biscuits

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: Essential oils (orange, lemon) or extracts (bitter almond, coffee, vanilla)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 100°C (215°F), Gas Mark ¼. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. In a large bowl, use an electric handheld mixer to whisk the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt. Add the caster sugar all at once and continue to whisk on a low speed for a few moments. Slowly add the icing sugar. The meringue should be dense and shiny.
Divide the meringue between several bowls. Use food colouring and extracts to colour and flavour each portion according to your fancy.
Transfer the coloured meringue mixtures into piping bags with fluted nozzles. Pipe pretty rosettes onto the baking tray, leaving plenty of room between them.
Dry out the meringues in the oven for 1½ hours until they are firm and dry to the touch. Let them cool on a wire rack.

recipes.searchText: Colourful Mini Meringues Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 3 egg whites A pinch of salt 100g caster sugar 120g icing sugar Food colouring Essential oils (orange, lemon) or extracts (bitter almond, coffee, vanilla) Preheat the oven to 100°C (215°F), Gas Mark ¼. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. In a large bowl, use an electric handheld mixer to whisk the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt. Add the caster sugar all at once and continue to whisk on a low speed for a few moments. Slowly add the icing sugar. The meringue should be dense and shiny. Divide the meringue between several bowls. Use food colouring and extracts to colour and flavour each portion according to your fancy. Transfer the coloured meringue mixtures into piping bags with fluted nozzles. Pipe pretty rosettes onto the baking tray, leaving plenty of room between them. Dry out the meringues in the oven for 1½ hours until they are firm and dry to the touch. Let them cool on a wire rack.
recipes.title: Colourful Mini Meringues

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease 10–12 small oval moulds. Grate the zest of 1 orange. Juice both oranges. Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt.

In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the ground almonds, orange juice and zest. Incorporate the flour, then fold in the egg whites with a rubber spatula.

Pour the batter into the moulds and bake for 10 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 160°C (325°F), Gas Mark 3, and bake for another 10–12 minutes. Allow the cakes to cool, remove them from their moulds and spread the marmalade on top. Decorate with the almonds.

recipes.searchText: Mini Orange and Almond Cakes Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 2 unwaxed oranges 4 eggs A pinch of salt 200g caster sugar 200g ground almonds 40g plain flour Butter for greasing 6 tablespoons orange marmalade 50g almonds Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease 10–12 small oval moulds. Grate the zest of 1 orange. Juice both oranges. Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks with the salt. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the ground almonds, orange juice and zest. Incorporate the flour, then fold in the egg whites with a rubber spatula. Pour the batter into the moulds and bake for 10 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 160°C (325°F), Gas Mark 3, and bake for another 10–12 minutes. Allow the cakes to cool, remove them from their moulds and spread the marmalade on top. Decorate with the almonds.
recipes.title: Mini Orange and Almond Cakes

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4, and liberally grease some small cake tins. Set 20g of walnuts aside for the decoration and roughly chop the rest in a food processor.

Separate the egg whites from the egg yolks. Use an electric handheld mixer to whisk together the egg yolks and sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the cornflour and chopped walnuts and mix well with a wooden spoon.

Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks. Take 2 tablespoons of the egg whites and mix them vigorously into the walnut batter to lighten it. Fold in the rest of the egg whites carefully, to avoid deflating them.

Pour the mixture into the tins. Bake in the middle of the oven for 10 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 150°C (300°F), Gas Mark 2. Continue to bake for another 10–12 minutes. Ensure the cakes are cooked by piercing one with a sharp knife: the blade should come out dry. Let the cakes rest for 5 minutes before removing them from their tins. Allow them to cool on a wire rack.

Prepare the icing: mix the icing sugar with the measured water, add the instant coffee and mix well until you get a thick but runny paste. Spread it over the cakes with a rubber spatula. Decorate the tops with the whole walnuts.

recipes.searchText: Mini Walnut Delights Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients For the icing Butter, for greasing 120g walnuts 3 eggs 130g caster sugar 75g cornflour 80g icing sugar 1 tablespoon water 1 teaspoon freeze-dried instant coffee Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4, and liberally grease some small cake tins. Set 20g of walnuts aside for the decoration and roughly chop the rest in a food processor. Separate the egg whites from the egg yolks. Use an electric handheld mixer to whisk together the egg yolks and sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the cornflour and chopped walnuts and mix well with a wooden spoon. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks. Take 2 tablespoons of the egg whites and mix them vigorously into the walnut batter to lighten it. Fold in the rest of the egg whites carefully, to avoid deflating them. Pour the mixture into the tins. Bake in the middle of the oven for 10 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 150°C (300°F), Gas Mark 2. Continue to bake for another 10–12 minutes. Ensure the cakes are cooked by piercing one with a sharp knife: the blade should come out dry. Let the cakes rest for 5 minutes before removing them from their tins. Allow them to cool on a wire rack. Prepare the icing: mix the icing sugar with the measured water, add the instant coffee and mix well until you get a thick but runny paste. Spread it over the cakes with a rubber spatula. Decorate the tops with the whole walnuts.
recipes.title: Mini Walnut Delights

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Melt the butter.

In a large bowl, combine the sugars and sift in the flour. Add the eggs (one at a time) and salt, and mix with a wooden spoon. Incorporate the melted butter and flaked almonds (mix them in gently so as not to break them).

Use a little spoon to scoop small dollops of batter onto the baking paper, leaving plenty of space between them. Spread each dollop lightly with the back of a wet fork, dipping it in cold water between each one. Bake for about 4 minutes.

Remove the baking tray from the oven and, using a palette knife, quickly lift the biscuits from the tray while they’re still soft. Place 3 or 4 of them at a time on a rolling pin (or empty bottle). Once they’ve hardened, remove them from the rolling pin and place them in a sealable container.

recipes.searchText: Almond Tuiles Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 75g butter 100g caster sugar 3.5g (1 level teaspoon) vanilla sugar 75g plain flour 2 eggs A pinch of salt 75g flaked almonds Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Melt the butter. In a large bowl, combine the sugars and sift in the flour. Add the eggs (one at a time) and salt, and mix with a wooden spoon. Incorporate the melted butter and flaked almonds (mix them in gently so as not to break them). Use a little spoon to scoop small dollops of batter onto the baking paper, leaving plenty of space between them. Spread each dollop lightly with the back of a wet fork, dipping it in cold water between each one. Bake for about 4 minutes. Remove the baking tray from the oven and, using a palette knife, quickly lift the biscuits from the tray while they’re still soft. Place 3 or 4 of them at a time on a rolling pin (or empty bottle). Once they’ve hardened, remove them from the rolling pin and place them in a sealable container.
recipes.title: Almond Tuiles

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper.
Melt the butter over a bain-marie. In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugars, egg whites and melted butter.

Using a piping bag or a spoon, spoon the batter on to the baking paper in 8cm discs. Bake for 8–10 minutes. Once the biscuits have begun to brown around the edges, remove them from the oven and use a palette knife to remove the discs from the tray quickly while they’re still soft. Immediately roll them up tightly or over a wooden stick. Allow them to cool completely and store them in a sealed container.

recipes.searchText: Cigarette Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 100g butter 90g plain flour 160g caster sugar 7.5g (1 heaped teaspoon) vanilla sugar 4 egg whites Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Melt the butter over a bain-marie. In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugars, egg whites and melted butter. Using a piping bag or a spoon, spoon the batter on to the baking paper in 8cm discs. Bake for 8–10 minutes. Once the biscuits have begun to brown around the edges, remove them from the oven and use a palette knife to remove the discs from the tray quickly while they’re still soft. Immediately roll them up tightly or over a wooden stick. Allow them to cool completely and store them in a sealed container.
recipes.title: Cigarette Biscuits

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 225g butter, at room temperature, cut into pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F), Gas Mark 2. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Sift the flour onto a work surface, then add the salt and butter. Knead until the dough becomes smooth and even.

Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1cm and cut it into little discs with a pastry cutter. Place the discs on the baking tray and dust the tops with sugar. Bake for 30 minutes. The shortbread should not brown. Store the biscuits in a sealed container. Serving suggestion These biscuits are intentionally low in sugar and are great accompaniments to ice cream, sorbet and fruit salads.

recipes.searchText: Shortbread Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 250g plain flour ½ teaspoon salt 225g butter, at room temperature, cut into pieces 40g caster sugar Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F), Gas Mark 2. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Sift the flour onto a work surface, then add the salt and butter. Knead until the dough becomes smooth and even. Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1cm and cut it into little discs with a pastry cutter. Place the discs on the baking tray and dust the tops with sugar. Bake for 30 minutes. The shortbread should not brown. Store the biscuits in a sealed container. Serving suggestion These biscuits are intentionally low in sugar and are great accompaniments to ice cream, sorbet and fruit salads.
recipes.title: Shortbread Biscuits

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Macerate the currants in the rum for 1 hour.

Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. In a large bowl, whisk the butter with the caster sugar. Add the eggs one by one and mix well. Pour in the flour and add the currants, rum and salt, mixing well before adding each new ingredient.
Place small spoonfuls of dough onto the baking paper, leaving plenty of space between them. Bake for 10 minutes. Once the biscuits have cooled, store them in a sealed container.

recipes.searchText: Rum and Currant Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 80g currants 80ml rum 125g butter, at room temperature 125g caster sugar 2 eggs 150g plain flour A pinch of salt Macerate the currants in the rum for 1 hour. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. In a large bowl, whisk the butter with the caster sugar. Add the eggs one by one and mix well. Pour in the flour and add the currants, rum and salt, mixing well before adding each new ingredient. Place small spoonfuls of dough onto the baking paper, leaving plenty of space between them. Bake for 10 minutes. Once the biscuits have cooled, store them in a sealed container.
recipes.title: Rum and Currant Biscuits

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper.

Prepare the dough: sift the flour. Grate the lemon zest. In a large bowl, mix together the butter and caster sugar until creamy. Add the egg and the lemon zest. Gradually add the flour while stirring continuously, then finish by kneading the mixture by hand.
Roll the dough out to a thickness of 8mm. Using a pastry cutter, cut out hearts, discs or diamond shapes. Place them on the baking tray and bake for 10 minutes.
Remove the biscuits from the tray, place them on a wire rack and let them cool.
Spread lemon curd on top of half the biscuits. Top them with the remaining biscuits and sprinkle them with icing sugar. Spoon some more lemon curd on top of each biscuit and serve immediately.

recipes.searchText: Lemon Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients For the dough 300g lemon curd Icing sugar, for dusting 175g plain flour 1 unwaxed lemon 80g butter 150g caster sugar 1 egg Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Prepare the dough: sift the flour. Grate the lemon zest. In a large bowl, mix together the butter and caster sugar until creamy. Add the egg and the lemon zest. Gradually add the flour while stirring continuously, then finish by kneading the mixture by hand. Roll the dough out to a thickness of 8mm. Using a pastry cutter, cut out hearts, discs or diamond shapes. Place them on the baking tray and bake for 10 minutes. Remove the biscuits from the tray, place them on a wire rack and let them cool. Spread lemon curd on top of half the biscuits. Top them with the remaining biscuits and sprinkle them with icing sugar. Spoon some more lemon curd on top of each biscuit and serve immediately.
recipes.title: Lemon Biscuits

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a large bowl, combine the butter, caster sugar, 3 egg yolks and salt. Mix until creamy. Gradually add the flour and half the milk until the dough is pliable but not soft. Roll it into a ball and allow it to rest for 30 minutes in a cool place.
Preheat the oven to 220°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Grease a baking tray. Roll out the dough to a thickness of 4mm. Use a heart-shaped pastry cutter to cut out the biscuits. Place them on the baking tray.
Whisk the final egg yolk with the remaining milk. Use a brush to coat the biscuits with the egg wash. Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the biscuits are lightly browned.
Remove the biscuits from the oven and let them cool on a wire rack. Store in a sealed container.

recipes.searchText: French Butter Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 200g butter + extra for greasing 100g caster sugar 4 egg yolks 320g plain flour 100ml milk A pinch of salt In a large bowl, combine the butter, caster sugar, 3 egg yolks and salt. Mix until creamy. Gradually add the flour and half the milk until the dough is pliable but not soft. Roll it into a ball and allow it to rest for 30 minutes in a cool place. Preheat the oven to 220°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Grease a baking tray. Roll out the dough to a thickness of 4mm. Use a heart-shaped pastry cutter to cut out the biscuits. Place them on the baking tray. Whisk the final egg yolk with the remaining milk. Use a brush to coat the biscuits with the egg wash. Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the biscuits are lightly browned. Remove the biscuits from the oven and let them cool on a wire rack. Store in a sealed container.
recipes.title: French Butter Biscuits

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Refrigerate the egg whites the night before making the macarons.
Prepare the ganache: melt the chocolate over a bain-marie.
Add the single cream and mix the ganache with a spatula until smooth. Refrigerate the mixture.
The following day, preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F), Gas Mark 3. Combine the icing sugar and the ground almonds. Spread the mixture on to a baking tray. Bake for 5–10 minutes in order to dry it out.
Whisk the chilled egg whites into very stiff peaks in a large bowl, gradually adding the caster sugar while continuing to whisk.
Add the cocoa powder to the ground almond mixture.
Use a spatula to stir the cocoa powder mixture carefully into the egg white mixture.
Pour the mixture into a piping bag with a smooth nozzle.
Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Pipe small, round, equal- sized discs of batter on to the baking tray.

Allow the macarons to stand for 20 minutes, then bake for 12–15 minutes. Let the macarons rest for a few minutes when they come out of the oven, then trickle a little water on to the nonstick baking paper in order to detach them more easily.
Use a spatula to mix the chilled ganache, then pipe it on to half of the macarons. Cover with the remaining macaron discs. Keep refrigerated.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Macarons Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients For The Ganache 4 egg whites 220g icing sugar 120g ground almonds 50g caster sugar 30g cocoa powder 175g dark chocolate 300ml single cream Refrigerate the egg whites the night before making the macarons. Prepare the ganache: melt the chocolate over a bain-marie. Add the single cream and mix the ganache with a spatula until smooth. Refrigerate the mixture. The following day, preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F), Gas Mark 3. Combine the icing sugar and the ground almonds. Spread the mixture on to a baking tray. Bake for 5–10 minutes in order to dry it out. Whisk the chilled egg whites into very stiff peaks in a large bowl, gradually adding the caster sugar while continuing to whisk. Add the cocoa powder to the ground almond mixture. Use a spatula to stir the cocoa powder mixture carefully into the egg white mixture. Pour the mixture into a piping bag with a smooth nozzle. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Pipe small, round, equal- sized discs of batter on to the baking tray. Allow the macarons to stand for 20 minutes, then bake for 12–15 minutes. Let the macarons rest for a few minutes when they come out of the oven, then trickle a little water on to the nonstick baking paper in order to detach them more easily. Use a spatula to mix the chilled ganache, then pipe it on to half of the macarons. Cover with the remaining macaron discs. Keep refrigerated.
recipes.title: Chocolate Macarons

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Whip the butter and icing sugar into a light cream. In a separate bowl, sift in the flour and baking powder with the ground almonds, then fold in the butter mixture with a spatula. Add the egg and vanilla extract and whisk until the mixture is evenly combined. Knead the dough into a ball. Wrap it in clingfilm and refrigerate it for 1 hour.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Roll the dough out to a thickness of 5mm and use a pastry cutter of your choice to cut out the biscuits. Use a smaller pastry cutter to cut the centre out of half the biscuits.
Arrange all the biscuits on the baking tray and bake for 5–10 minutes, depending on how thick the biscuits are. Allow them to cool on a wire rack.

Spread the jams over the whole biscuits, alternating between strawberry and apricot, leaving a margin around the edges. Dust icing sugar over the biscuits with holes in them and place them on top of the jam-covered ones.

recipes.searchText: Jam Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 140g butter, at room temperature 50g icing sugar 140g plain flour 6g (about 1 teaspoon) baking powder 30g ground almonds 1 egg 1 tablespoon vanilla extract 50g strawberry jam 50g apricot jam Icing sugar, for dusting Whip the butter and icing sugar into a light cream. In a separate bowl, sift in the flour and baking powder with the ground almonds, then fold in the butter mixture with a spatula. Add the egg and vanilla extract and whisk until the mixture is evenly combined. Knead the dough into a ball. Wrap it in clingfilm and refrigerate it for 1 hour. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Roll the dough out to a thickness of 5mm and use a pastry cutter of your choice to cut out the biscuits. Use a smaller pastry cutter to cut the centre out of half the biscuits. Arrange all the biscuits on the baking tray and bake for 5–10 minutes, depending on how thick the biscuits are. Allow them to cool on a wire rack. Spread the jams over the whole biscuits, alternating between strawberry and apricot, leaving a margin around the edges. Dust icing sugar over the biscuits with holes in them and place them on top of the jam-covered ones.
recipes.title: Jam Biscuits

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the butter and mix well. Finally, sift in the flour and baking powder and mix well until combined.
Roll the dough into a ball using your hands and wrap it in clingfilm. Refrigerate it for at least 1 hour.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Roll the dough out to a thickness of 1cm on a sheet of nonstick baking paper. Cut out the biscuits with a round pastry cutter.
Arrange the biscuits on the baking tray and bake for 15 minutes. Allow them to cool on a wire rack.

recipes.searchText: Breton Biscuits Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 2 egg yolks 75g caster sugar 80g salted butter, at room temperature 120g plain flour 1 teaspoon baking powder Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the butter and mix well. Finally, sift in the flour and baking powder and mix well until combined. Roll the dough into a ball using your hands and wrap it in clingfilm. Refrigerate it for at least 1 hour. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Roll the dough out to a thickness of 1cm on a sheet of nonstick baking paper. Cut out the biscuits with a round pastry cutter. Arrange the biscuits on the baking tray and bake for 15 minutes. Allow them to cool on a wire rack.
recipes.title: Breton Biscuits

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100g dark chocolate or milk chocolate (or a combination), chopped into small

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Sift the flour with the baking powder and salt. In a large bowl, combine the butter and sugars and whisk until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the egg and whisk again. Incorporate the flour, then add the chocolate with a spatula and mix well.
Place the dough on a large rectangle of clingfilm and shape it into a 5cm- wide sausage. Freeze for at least 1 hour.

Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Unwrap the dough and slice it into 8mm-thick disks. Place them on the baking tray. Bake for 8–10 minutes, no longer. Remove the cookies from the oven when they start to look done around the edges but remain soft in the middle. They’ll harden as they cool.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Chip Cookies Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 200g plain flour 1 teaspoon baking powder ½ teaspoon salt 150g butter, at room temperature 100g caster sugar 75g brown sugar 1 egg 100g dark chocolate or milk chocolate (or a combination), chopped into small pieces, or 100g chocolate chips Sift the flour with the baking powder and salt. In a large bowl, combine the butter and sugars and whisk until the mixture becomes pale in colour. Add the egg and whisk again. Incorporate the flour, then add the chocolate with a spatula and mix well. Place the dough on a large rectangle of clingfilm and shape it into a 5cm- wide sausage. Freeze for at least 1 hour. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Unwrap the dough and slice it into 8mm-thick disks. Place them on the baking tray. Bake for 8–10 minutes, no longer. Remove the cookies from the oven when they start to look done around the edges but remain soft in the middle. They’ll harden as they cool.
recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Roll out the puff pastry into a rectangle that is 3 times longer than it is wide. Dust the top with icing sugar. Fold it in 3 and allow it to rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator. Repeat the process.

Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Roll out the dough into a 1cm-thick rectangle. Dust the top with icing sugar. Refold each side toward the centre lengthways, then fold again until you have the shape of a sausage.
Cut the sausage into 7mm-thick slices. Place these on the baking tray, leaving plenty of space between them so they don’t stick to one another (the dough will expand during cooking).
Bake for 15–20 minutes, turning the palmiers halfway through so that both sides can caramelize.
Let them cool and store them in a sealed container so that they don’t soften.

recipes.searchText: Palmiers Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 500g all-butter puff pastry 150g icing sugar Roll out the puff pastry into a rectangle that is 3 times longer than it is wide. Dust the top with icing sugar. Fold it in 3 and allow it to rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator. Repeat the process. Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Roll out the dough into a 1cm-thick rectangle. Dust the top with icing sugar. Refold each side toward the centre lengthways, then fold again until you have the shape of a sausage. Cut the sausage into 7mm-thick slices. Place these on the baking tray, leaving plenty of space between them so they don’t stick to one another (the dough will expand during cooking). Bake for 15–20 minutes, turning the palmiers halfway through so that both sides can caramelize. Let them cool and store them in a sealed container so that they don’t soften.
recipes.title: Palmiers

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the dough: in a large bowl, combine the flour and the salt, then make a well in the centre. Pour in the butter, honey and 1 tablespoon water. Mix while bringing the flour in from the edges as you work. Knead thoroughly, adding a little more water as needed. Let the dough rest for 1 hour at room temperature.

Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F), Gas Mark 2. Line a baking sheet with nonstick baking paper. Prepare the filling: combine the ground almonds with the sugar and salt. Add the butter and orange blossom water. Mix until soft. Shape the filling into 15 finger-sized sausages.

Divide the dough into 2 or 3 portions. Roll out on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 2mm. Place a filling piece 5cm from the edge and fold the dough over it. Press down on the sides to seal the dough edges together, then cut off any excess dough with a pizza cutter or sharp knife. Curve the resulting turnover into a half-moon shape. Repeat until all the filling pieces have been wrapped in dough.

Brush the gazelle horns with the egg yolk mixed with 1 tablespoon water, then scatter the flaked almonds on a plate and press the horns into them. Place the horns on the baking tray and pierce them all the way through in 3 places. Bake for 10–15 minutes.

recipes.searchText: Almond Gazelle Horns Biscuits & small cakes For the dough For the filling For the decoration 250g plain flour + extra for dusting A pinch of salt 2 tablespoons melted butter 1 tablespoon honey 250g ground almonds 100g caster sugar A pinch of salt 2 tablespoons melted butter 2 tablespoons orange blossom water 1 egg yolk Flaked almonds Prepare the dough: in a large bowl, combine the flour and the salt, then make a well in the centre. Pour in the butter, honey and 1 tablespoon water. Mix while bringing the flour in from the edges as you work. Knead thoroughly, adding a little more water as needed. Let the dough rest for 1 hour at room temperature. Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F), Gas Mark 2. Line a baking sheet with nonstick baking paper. Prepare the filling: combine the ground almonds with the sugar and salt. Add the butter and orange blossom water. Mix until soft. Shape the filling into 15 finger-sized sausages. Divide the dough into 2 or 3 portions. Roll out on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 2mm. Place a filling piece 5cm from the edge and fold the dough over it. Press down on the sides to seal the dough edges together, then cut off any excess dough with a pizza cutter or sharp knife. Curve the resulting turnover into a half-moon shape. Repeat until all the filling pieces have been wrapped in dough. Brush the gazelle horns with the egg yolk mixed with 1 tablespoon water, then scatter the flaked almonds on a plate and press the horns into them. Place the horns on the baking tray and pierce them all the way through in 3 places. Bake for 10–15 minutes.
recipes.title: Almond Gazelle Horns

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5 apples, preferably reinettes, peeled, cored and diced
500g all-butter puff pastry (or 2 rolls of ready-rolled dough)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 250°C (485°F), Gas Mark 9. Line a baking sheet with nonstick baking paper. As soon as they are cut, mix the apples with the lemon juice to prevent them from browning. Drain them and mix them with the caster sugar and double cream in a large bowl.
Roll out the puff pastry and cut out ten to twelve 12cm discs. Whisk the egg and brush some of it along the edges of the dough discs.

Arrange pieces of apple and butter on one half of each disc. Fold the other side over the filling to create turnovers. Seal the edges by pressing down with your fingers. Brush the top of the pastry with the rest of the egg. Allow the egg wash to dry, then use the tip of a knife to make a criss-cross pattern on the top of the turnovers, taking care not to pierce through the dough.
Bake for 10 minutes. Reduce the temperature to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6, and continue to bake for another 25–30 minutes. Serve warm.

recipes.searchText: Apple Turnovers Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 5 apples, preferably reinettes, peeled, cored and diced 2 tablespoons lemon juice 150g caster sugar 1–2 tablespoons double cream 500g all-butter puff pastry (or 2 rolls of ready-rolled dough) 1 egg 30g butter, cut into small pieces Preheat the oven to 250°C (485°F), Gas Mark 9. Line a baking sheet with nonstick baking paper. As soon as they are cut, mix the apples with the lemon juice to prevent them from browning. Drain them and mix them with the caster sugar and double cream in a large bowl. Roll out the puff pastry and cut out ten to twelve 12cm discs. Whisk the egg and brush some of it along the edges of the dough discs. Arrange pieces of apple and butter on one half of each disc. Fold the other side over the filling to create turnovers. Seal the edges by pressing down with your fingers. Brush the top of the pastry with the rest of the egg. Allow the egg wash to dry, then use the tip of a knife to make a criss-cross pattern on the top of the turnovers, taking care not to pierce through the dough. Bake for 10 minutes. Reduce the temperature to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6, and continue to bake for another 25–30 minutes. Serve warm.
recipes.title: Apple Turnovers

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the leavening: dissolve the yeast in 60ml of the milk and add 30g of the flour. Mix well. Sprinkle another 30g of flour on top and let the mixture rise for 30 minutes in a warm place.
Soak the currants in a bowl of warm water, allowing them to swell.
Sift the remaining flour into a large bowl. Add the leavening, sugar, 3 eggs and salt. Knead for 5 minutes, hitting the dough on the table to make it more elastic.
Add the rest of the milk and mix well. Add the softened butter to the dough, then the drained currants. Knead for a bit longer and allow the dough to rest for 1 hour in a warm place.

Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape them into sausages, roll them into spirals and let them rise for 30 minutes on the baking tray.
Whisk the remaining egg with a fork. Brush the rolls with the egg, sprinkle them with pearl sugar and bake for 20 minutes. Serve warm or cold.

recipes.searchText: Raisin Rolls Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 15g fresh yeast 100ml milk 530g plain flour 100g currants 30g caster sugar 4 eggs 6 pinches of salt 150g butter, at room temperature Pearl sugar, to decorate Prepare the leavening: dissolve the yeast in 60ml of the milk and add 30g of the flour. Mix well. Sprinkle another 30g of flour on top and let the mixture rise for 30 minutes in a warm place. Soak the currants in a bowl of warm water, allowing them to swell. Sift the remaining flour into a large bowl. Add the leavening, sugar, 3 eggs and salt. Knead for 5 minutes, hitting the dough on the table to make it more elastic. Add the rest of the milk and mix well. Add the softened butter to the dough, then the drained currants. Knead for a bit longer and allow the dough to rest for 1 hour in a warm place. Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F), Gas Mark 6. Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape them into sausages, roll them into spirals and let them rise for 30 minutes on the baking tray. Whisk the remaining egg with a fork. Brush the rolls with the egg, sprinkle them with pearl sugar and bake for 20 minutes. Serve warm or cold.
recipes.title: Raisin Rolls

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dough
lines: 75g butter, at room temperature + extra for greasing

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Warm the milk and dissolve the yeast in it. Allow it to rest for 10 minutes.

Pour the flour onto a work surface and make a well in the centre. Fill it with the dissolved yeast, egg, salt, caster sugar and butter. Knead everything for at least 10 minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic (you can do this by hand, with a food processor equipped with a dough hook or with a bread machine).
Place the dough in a large bowl, cover it with a tea towel and allow it to rise for about 1½ hours in a hot place (close to a radiator, if it’s winter) until it doubles in volume.

Punch down the dough and knead it lightly. Grease a gratin dish. Cover your hands with flour and shape the dough into mandarin-sized balls. Place them in the dish, spacing them out a little. Let them rise again for 1½ hours.

Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F), Gas Mark 6. Prepare the topping: mix the milk with the icing sugar and brush the mixture over the buns. Use a pair of scissors to score each bun with an X and bake for 20 minutes. Serve the buns warm to your taste. KNOW YOUR SPICES, herbs and flowers! Herbs, flowers and spices are your allies when it comes to flavouring your desserts. They bring added flavour and a touch of originality. ices Ginger: this is a key ingredient in gingerbread. In powdered form, it can be sprinkled over jams and tarts. When fresh, it pairs very well with rhubarb (compote or jam). Cardamom: crush the seeds from 1–2 pods and add them to rice pudding or semolina. Pepper: this is great for bringing out the flavour in fruit. For example, you can grind some pepper over strawberries or drop a few peppercorns in a poached pear syrup. Chilli: mix a little fresh red chilli pepper with sugar to flavour mango or pineapple slices like they do in Mexico. Espelette chilli pepper also goes very well with chocolate. Add a small pinch of it the next time you make a mousse. herbs Most of the time, these are infused in hot liquid: A sugar syrup infused with a handful of basil, lemon verbena or the leaves of 3–4 sprigs of mint for 30 minutes will make a base for a delicious sorbet. An infusion with milk will make a great addition to a crème anglaise for an ice cream or ice cream float. Steam some herbs by adding them to the water in which you’re cooking fruit – lemon verbena pairs well with figs, for example. Herbs also go very well with fruit: Rosemary: slip about 20 leaves into a tarte Tatin or a classic apple tart, but not more than that, as rosemary has a very strong flavour. Thyme: this is delicious with apples, apricots or peaches. Lemon verbena: add this to a summer peach soup. As for jams: the leaves of 1–2 sprigs of rosemary or thyme are enough for one pan of jam. For less flavourful herbs, such as lemon verbena, lime or mint, use about 30 leaves. flowers Blossom waters: orange blossom or rose waters add delicate flavours to creams and crêpe batters – use a ratio of 1 tablespoon per 500ml liquid. Lavender: this goes well with peaches and apricots. Add flavour to ice cream by mixing 500ml crème anglaise with 1 tablespoon dried flowers, or to sorbet by adding 500ml syrup. Hibiscus: this gives crème anglaise a nice pink or red colour depending on the amount used. Soak the dried leaves in milk before preparing the crème anglaise. Acacia or wisteria: for a dessert with a subtle flavour, dip these flowers in a light doughnut batter and fry them.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300g butter, at room temperature, cut into small pieces + extra for greasing

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Warm the milk and dissolve the yeast in it. Sift the flour over a large bowl and make a well in the centre. Fill it with the eggs, salt and caster sugar and mix together well. Add the butter and dissolved yeast, then vigorously knead the dough.
Generously grease 6 small brioche moulds and divide the dough between them. Let them rise for 1 hour in a warm place.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Bake the cakes for 20 minutes. Let the cakes cool a little, then serve warm. Serving suggestion Serve these cakes with chocolate mousse or a fruit compote.

recipes.searchText: Soft Brioche Buns Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 100ml milk 15g fresh yeast 300g plain flour 4 eggs A pinch of salt 20g caster sugar 300g butter, at room temperature, cut into small pieces + extra for greasing Warm the milk and dissolve the yeast in it. Sift the flour over a large bowl and make a well in the centre. Fill it with the eggs, salt and caster sugar and mix together well. Add the butter and dissolved yeast, then vigorously knead the dough. Generously grease 6 small brioche moulds and divide the dough between them. Let them rise for 1 hour in a warm place. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Bake the cakes for 20 minutes. Let the cakes cool a little, then serve warm. Serving suggestion Serve these cakes with chocolate mousse or a fruit compote.
recipes.title: Soft Brioche Buns

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 30g butter, cut into small pieces + extra for greasing
A pinch of bicarbonate of soda

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F), Gas Mark 7. Grease a baking sheet. Place the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the butter and rub in with your fingertips.

Combine the bicarbonate of soda with the caster sugar and add it to the flour and butter mixture. Mix well. Pour in the buttermilk and continue to mix until the dough is nice and thick. Place the dough on a lightly floured work surface and knead until it becomes pliable.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1.5cm. Divide the dough into 8 parts, then cut each section into triangles.
Arrange the triangles on the baking sheet and bake for about 20 minutes, until the scones have lightly browned. Remove them from the oven and place them on a serving dish. Serve warm.

recipes.searchText: Buttermilk Scones Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 30g butter, cut into small pieces + extra for greasing 250g plain flour + extra for dusting A pinch of salt A pinch of bicarbonate of soda 20g caster sugar 100ml buttermilk Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F), Gas Mark 7. Grease a baking sheet. Place the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the butter and rub in with your fingertips. Combine the bicarbonate of soda with the caster sugar and add it to the flour and butter mixture. Mix well. Pour in the buttermilk and continue to mix until the dough is nice and thick. Place the dough on a lightly floured work surface and knead until it becomes pliable. Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1.5cm. Divide the dough into 8 parts, then cut each section into triangles. Arrange the triangles on the baking sheet and bake for about 20 minutes, until the scones have lightly browned. Remove them from the oven and place them on a serving dish. Serve warm.
recipes.title: Buttermilk Scones

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Place a small bowl over a bain-marie and add the chocolate.
Pour in the milk and stir until the chocolate is completely melted and smooth.
Gradually add the butter pieces.
Add the egg yolks, one at a time.
Add the double cream and the icing sugar.
You have the option to add flavouring: rum, cognac or another liqueur of your choice. Whisk the mixture for 5 minutes.
Spread the mixture on a baking tray lined with nonstick baking paper to a thickness of about 2cm. Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Dust the cocoa powder on to a large plate or on to a baking tray.
Cut the refrigerated chocolate into small squares.
Dip your hands into the cocoa powder, pick up a chocolate square, quickly roll it into a ball and immediately roll it in the cocoa powder. Work swiftly to prevent the truffles from softening.
Once all the truffles are made, remove them from the cocoa powder and place them in a cup. Keep them in a cool place (but not in the refrigerator) until serving.

recipes.searchText: Dark Chocolate Truffles Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 300g dark chocolate, broken into pieces 1 tablespoon milk 100g butter, cut into small pieces 2 egg yolks 50ml double cream 125g icing sugar 1 tablespoon liqueur of your choice (optional) 250g bitter cocoa powder Place a small bowl over a bain-marie and add the chocolate. Pour in the milk and stir until the chocolate is completely melted and smooth. Gradually add the butter pieces. Add the egg yolks, one at a time. Add the double cream and the icing sugar. You have the option to add flavouring: rum, cognac or another liqueur of your choice. Whisk the mixture for 5 minutes. Spread the mixture on a baking tray lined with nonstick baking paper to a thickness of about 2cm. Refrigerate for 2 hours. Dust the cocoa powder on to a large plate or on to a baking tray. Cut the refrigerated chocolate into small squares. Dip your hands into the cocoa powder, pick up a chocolate square, quickly roll it into a ball and immediately roll it in the cocoa powder. Work swiftly to prevent the truffles from softening. Once all the truffles are made, remove them from the cocoa powder and place them in a cup. Keep them in a cool place (but not in the refrigerator) until serving.
recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Truffles

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Line a baking sheet with nonstick baking paper. Place a rectangular dessert ring (or a 22cm round cake ring) on the baking sheet. Lightly grease it using a brush.

In a saucepan, combine the sugar, double cream, honey and cocoa powder. Heat while stirring with a wooden spoon until the caramel turns dark amber. Pour the caramel into the dessert ring and allow it to cool. Remove the ring and cut the caramel into squares.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Caramels Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 1 tablespoon sunflower oil, for greasing 250g caster sugar 100g double cream 50g honey 50g cocoa powder Line a baking sheet with nonstick baking paper. Place a rectangular dessert ring (or a 22cm round cake ring) on the baking sheet. Lightly grease it using a brush. In a saucepan, combine the sugar, double cream, honey and cocoa powder. Heat while stirring with a wooden spoon until the caramel turns dark amber. Pour the caramel into the dessert ring and allow it to cool. Remove the ring and cut the caramel into squares.
recipes.title: Chocolate Caramels

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Whisk the eggs with the milk, vanilla extract and half the sugar.
Dip the bread in this mixture.

Melt the butter in a frying pan with the remaining sugar. Lightly brown the soaked bread slices on each side and serve immediately. Serving suggestion Serve for brunch with some fresh fruit, chocolate sauce or dulce de leche.

recipes.searchText: Pain Perdu Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 2 eggs 400ml milk 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 4 tablespoons caster sugar 8 slices of stale bread (or brioche) 20g butter Whisk the eggs with the milk, vanilla extract and half the sugar. Dip the bread in this mixture. Melt the butter in a frying pan with the remaining sugar. Lightly brown the soaked bread slices on each side and serve immediately. Serving suggestion Serve for brunch with some fresh fruit, chocolate sauce or dulce de leche.
recipes.title: Pain Perdu

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan or in the microwave. In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and caster sugar. Mix well. Add the egg and milk and mix again. Add the melted butter.

Grease a hot frying pan with the oil using a piece of kitchen paper. Pour in large spoonfuls of batter, leaving plenty of space between them. Cook over a medium heat until the tops of the pancakes have set and flip them with a spatula until lightly browned on the other side (about 2 minutes per side). Remove the pancakes from the pan as soon as they’re cooked.

Keep the pancakes warm and repeat the process until all the batter is gone, greasing the pan in between each batch. Serving suggestion Serve these pancakes warm with butter, jam or maple syrup. ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 apples (preferably Belle de Boskoop or King of the Pippins), peeled, cored and thickly sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the fritter batter: in a large bowl, combine the flour and salt. Make a well in the centre and crack the egg into it, then add the oil. Mix well using a whisk, gradually adding the beer as you stir. Let the batter rest for at least 1 hour in the refrigerator.
Prepare the cinnamon sugar: combine the caster sugar with the cinnamon on a flat plate. Dip each apple slice into the cinnamon sugar, making sure the sugar sticks well.

Heat the cooking oil to 175°C (350°F). Use a long-stemmed fork to lift each apple slice and dip it in the fritter batter, then plunge it into the hot oil. Cook the fritters for about 4 minutes, turning them with a slotted spoon halfway through the cooking time. Once they’re lightly browned, remove them from the oil and place them on kitchen paper to soak up excess oil. Place them on a serving dish and serve immediately.

recipes.searchText: Cinnamon and Apple Fritters Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients For the fritter batter For the cinnamon sugar 4 apples (preferably Belle de Boskoop or King of the Pippins), peeled, cored and thickly sliced Sunflower oil for frying 125g plain flour ½ teaspoon salt 1 egg 1 tablespoon groundnut oil 150ml beer 45g caster sugar 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon Prepare the fritter batter: in a large bowl, combine the flour and salt. Make a well in the centre and crack the egg into it, then add the oil. Mix well using a whisk, gradually adding the beer as you stir. Let the batter rest for at least 1 hour in the refrigerator. Prepare the cinnamon sugar: combine the caster sugar with the cinnamon on a flat plate. Dip each apple slice into the cinnamon sugar, making sure the sugar sticks well. Heat the cooking oil to 175°C (350°F). Use a long-stemmed fork to lift each apple slice and dip it in the fritter batter, then plunge it into the hot oil. Cook the fritters for about 4 minutes, turning them with a slotted spoon halfway through the cooking time. Once they’re lightly browned, remove them from the oil and place them on kitchen paper to soak up excess oil. Place them on a serving dish and serve immediately.
recipes.title: Cinnamon and Apple Fritters

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the choux pastry: add the measured water, milk, salt, caster sugar and butter to a heavy-based saucepan and bring to the boil. Add the flour all at once and mix vigorously with a wooden spoon until the batter is smooth and even. Once it begins to come away from the sides, lower the heat and continue to stir for 2–3 minutes in order to cook it down. Remove from the heat and allow the dough to cool a bit. Add the eggs, one at a time, while continuing to stir until smooth.

Heat the cooking oil to 170–180°C (340–350°F). Use 2 small teaspoons to scoop out and shape about 10 walnut-sized balls of dough, then drop them in the oil. Cook for 2–3 minutes, turning them with a slotted spoon halfway through the cooking time. Once they’re lightly browned, remove them with the slotted spoon and place them on kitchen paper to soak up excess oil. Repeat the process until the dough has been used up.
Place the nuns’ puffs on a serving dish and dust them with icing sugar. Serve immediately or they’ll deflate – and they can’t be reheated.

recipes.searchText: Nuns’ Puffs Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients For the choux pastry Sunflower oil, for frying Icing sugar, for dusting 50ml water 60ml whole milk ½ teaspoon salt ½ teaspoon caster sugar 45g butter 60g plain flour 2 eggs Prepare the choux pastry: add the measured water, milk, salt, caster sugar and butter to a heavy-based saucepan and bring to the boil. Add the flour all at once and mix vigorously with a wooden spoon until the batter is smooth and even. Once it begins to come away from the sides, lower the heat and continue to stir for 2–3 minutes in order to cook it down. Remove from the heat and allow the dough to cool a bit. Add the eggs, one at a time, while continuing to stir until smooth. Heat the cooking oil to 170–180°C (340–350°F). Use 2 small teaspoons to scoop out and shape about 10 walnut-sized balls of dough, then drop them in the oil. Cook for 2–3 minutes, turning them with a slotted spoon halfway through the cooking time. Once they’re lightly browned, remove them with the slotted spoon and place them on kitchen paper to soak up excess oil. Repeat the process until the dough has been used up. Place the nuns’ puffs on a serving dish and dust them with icing sugar. Serve immediately or they’ll deflate – and they can’t be reheated.
recipes.title: Nuns’ Puffs

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: Sunflower oil (or grape seed oil), for frying

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the measured water to the boil with the butter, salt and 2 pinches of the caster sugar. Add the flour all at once and mix well with a wooden spoon until the mixture is thick and smooth.
Remove from the heat. Whisk the eggs, add them to the batter and mix well. Let the batter rest for 1 hour in a cool place.

Heat the oil to 180°C (355°F). Place the batter in a churro maker or in a piping bag with a fluted nozzle. Drop 10cm-long strips of batter into the oil, cutting the dough with scissors as it comes out of the nozzle. Do this in multiple batches so that the churros don’t stick to each other.

Cook the churros for 3–4 minutes, until golden brown, turning them halfway through the cooking time using a perforated spoon. Remove them from the oil and place them on kitchen paper to soak up excess oil. Dust the top with the remaining caster sugar and serve warm.

recipes.searchText: Churros Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 250ml water 60g butter A pinch of salt 60g caster sugar 225g plain flour 2 eggs Sunflower oil (or grape seed oil), for frying Bring the measured water to the boil with the butter, salt and 2 pinches of the caster sugar. Add the flour all at once and mix well with a wooden spoon until the mixture is thick and smooth. Remove from the heat. Whisk the eggs, add them to the batter and mix well. Let the batter rest for 1 hour in a cool place. Heat the oil to 180°C (355°F). Place the batter in a churro maker or in a piping bag with a fluted nozzle. Drop 10cm-long strips of batter into the oil, cutting the dough with scissors as it comes out of the nozzle. Do this in multiple batches so that the churros don’t stick to each other. Cook the churros for 3–4 minutes, until golden brown, turning them halfway through the cooking time using a perforated spoon. Remove them from the oil and place them on kitchen paper to soak up excess oil. Dust the top with the remaining caster sugar and serve warm.
recipes.title: Churros

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the waffle batter: bring the cream and half the milk to the boil in a saucepan. Allow it to cool. In a separate saucepan, bring the remaining milk to the boil with the salt. Add the flour and the butter. Cook the mixture down for 2–3 minutes while stirring with a spatula, as you would for a choux pastry. Pour this mixture into a large bowl, add the eggs, one by one, then the boiled milk and cream, and finally the orange blossom water. Mix well and let it cool completely. Allow the waffle batter to rest for at least 1 hour.
Use a brush dipped in oil to grease a handheld waffle iron, then preheat it. Pour a dollop of batter into one half of the open waffle iron, enough to fill it but not to make it overflow.
Close the waffle iron, then flip it upside down so that the batter can spread evenly across both sides. Cook on each side for 2 minutes. Remove the waffle from the iron and top it with icing sugar.

recipes.searchText: Waffles with Icing Sugar Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients For the waffle batter Oil for greasing Icing sugar 50ml single cream 200ml whole milk 3g (½ teaspoon) salt 75g plain flour 30g butter 3 eggs 1 teaspoon orange blossom water Prepare the waffle batter: bring the cream and half the milk to the boil in a saucepan. Allow it to cool. In a separate saucepan, bring the remaining milk to the boil with the salt. Add the flour and the butter. Cook the mixture down for 2–3 minutes while stirring with a spatula, as you would for a choux pastry. Pour this mixture into a large bowl, add the eggs, one by one, then the boiled milk and cream, and finally the orange blossom water. Mix well and let it cool completely. Allow the waffle batter to rest for at least 1 hour. Use a brush dipped in oil to grease a handheld waffle iron, then preheat it. Pour a dollop of batter into one half of the open waffle iron, enough to fill it but not to make it overflow. Close the waffle iron, then flip it upside down so that the batter can spread evenly across both sides. Cook on each side for 2 minutes. Remove the waffle from the iron and top it with icing sugar.
recipes.title: Waffles with Icing Sugar

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: Zest of ½ unwaxed lemon, very finely grated

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: The day before, sift the flour on to a work surface and make a well in the centre. Crack the eggs into the well and add the caster sugar, salt, oil and butter. Mix by hand, gradually incorporating the flour from the edges. Knead thoroughly, until the dough is smooth and no longer sticks to your fingers. Add the lemon zest and rum and knead for a few more minutes. Place the dough in a large bowl and allow it to rest in a cool place until the following day.

The following day, heat the oil to 180°C (355°F). Roll out the dough as thinly as possible on a lightly floured work surface. Cut through it with a serrated pizza wheel or with a sharp knife. Cut it in any shape you want.
Drop the pieces of dough into the hot oil, one by one. Avoid squeezing them so that they can puff out properly. Let them lightly brown, turning them once.
Drain the bugnes on a sheet of kitchen paper to soak up excess oil and dust them with icing sugar, if using. Serve hot or warm, accompanied by apricot jam, if you like.

recipes.searchText: Bugnes Biscuits & small cakes Ingredients 250g plain flour + extra for dusting 2 eggs 40g caster sugar 5g (1 teaspoon) salt 2 tablespoons sunflower oil 80g butter, at room temperature Zest of ½ unwaxed lemon, very finely grated 50ml dark rum Sunflower oil, for frying Icing sugar, for dusting (optional) Apricot jam, to serve (optional) The day before, sift the flour on to a work surface and make a well in the centre. Crack the eggs into the well and add the caster sugar, salt, oil and butter. Mix by hand, gradually incorporating the flour from the edges. Knead thoroughly, until the dough is smooth and no longer sticks to your fingers. Add the lemon zest and rum and knead for a few more minutes. Place the dough in a large bowl and allow it to rest in a cool place until the following day. The following day, heat the oil to 180°C (355°F). Roll out the dough as thinly as possible on a lightly floured work surface. Cut through it with a serrated pizza wheel or with a sharp knife. Cut it in any shape you want. Drop the pieces of dough into the hot oil, one by one. Avoid squeezing them so that they can puff out properly. Let them lightly brown, turning them once. Drain the bugnes on a sheet of kitchen paper to soak up excess oil and dust them with icing sugar, if using. Serve hot or warm, accompanied by apricot jam, if you like.
recipes.title: Bugnes

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 125g cold lightly salted butter, cut into pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pour the flour onto a worktop and make a well in the centre. Add the butter.
Combine the butter and flour by rubbing them together with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Add the water in 2 or 3 stages, mixing the dough as little as possible.
Quickly roll the dough into a ball. Small pieces of butter should still be visible. Wrap the dough in clingfilm and allow it to rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.

recipes.searchText: Shortcrust Pastry Baking workshop Ingredients 250g plain flour 125g cold lightly salted butter, cut into pieces 100ml cold water Pour the flour onto a worktop and make a well in the centre. Add the butter. Combine the butter and flour by rubbing them together with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the water in 2 or 3 stages, mixing the dough as little as possible. Quickly roll the dough into a ball. Small pieces of butter should still be visible. Wrap the dough in clingfilm and allow it to rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
recipes.title: Shortcrust Pastry

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Whisk together the butter, sugar, egg and salt – you’re not trying to obtain a smooth texture.
Add the flour and quickly finish mixing the dough by hand. Wrap it in clingfilm and allow it to rest in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.

Roll out the dough on a floured worktop, wrap it around the rolling pin and place it in the baking tin. Cut off the excess dough by passing the rolling pin over the edge of the tin. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Cover the dough with nonstick baking paper, weigh it down with baking beans (or dried beans) and bake blind for the time indicated in the recipe.

recipes.searchText: Sweet Shortcrust Pastry Baking workshop Ingredients 120g butter, at room temperature 60g caster sugar 1 egg 2 pinches of salt 220g plain flour + extra for dusting Whisk together the butter, sugar, egg and salt – you’re not trying to obtain a smooth texture. Add the flour and quickly finish mixing the dough by hand. Wrap it in clingfilm and allow it to rest in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight. Roll out the dough on a floured worktop, wrap it around the rolling pin and place it in the baking tin. Cut off the excess dough by passing the rolling pin over the edge of the tin. Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Cover the dough with nonstick baking paper, weigh it down with baking beans (or dried beans) and bake blind for the time indicated in the recipe.
recipes.title: Sweet Shortcrust Pastry

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 35g butter, at room temperature + 250g cold butter

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Place the flour, softened butter and salt on a work surface and add the measured water. Quickly mix together until the mixture is smooth and even.
Roll the dough into a ball, wrap it in clingfilm and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Place the cold butter between 2 sheets of nonstick baking paper and roll it out into a square of about 20cm.
Flour a worktop and roll out the dough into a rectangle measuring about 22 × 42cm, then place the butter at the top of the rectangle.
Fold the dough over the butter and pinch the edges closed.
Turn the dough a quarter of the way to the right and roll it out so that it’s 3 times longer than it is wide.
Fold the dough in 3 into the shape of an envelope.
Press down on the dough with your thumb to mark the completion of round one. Wrap the dough in clingfilm and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Repeat steps 6 and 7 and refrigerate the dough for 2 hours. Make two marks with your thumb to indicate completion of round two.
Repeat steps 6 and 7. The dough is now ready for use. Refrigerate it until you’re ready to use it.

recipes.searchText: Puff Pastry Baking workshop Ingredients 350g plain flour + extra for dusting 35g butter, at room temperature + 250g cold butter 1½ level teaspoons of salt 130ml water Place the flour, softened butter and salt on a work surface and add the measured water. Quickly mix together until the mixture is smooth and even. Roll the dough into a ball, wrap it in clingfilm and refrigerate for 2 hours. Place the cold butter between 2 sheets of nonstick baking paper and roll it out into a square of about 20cm. Flour a worktop and roll out the dough into a rectangle measuring about 22 × 42cm, then place the butter at the top of the rectangle. Fold the dough over the butter and pinch the edges closed. Turn the dough a quarter of the way to the right and roll it out so that it’s 3 times longer than it is wide. Fold the dough in 3 into the shape of an envelope. Press down on the dough with your thumb to mark the completion of round one. Wrap the dough in clingfilm and refrigerate for 2 hours. Repeat steps 6 and 7 and refrigerate the dough for 2 hours. Make two marks with your thumb to indicate completion of round two. Repeat steps 6 and 7. The dough is now ready for use. Refrigerate it until you’re ready to use it.
recipes.title: Puff Pastry

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 60g butter, at room temperature, cut into very small pieces
1 In a large bowl, whisk the egg with the icing sugar, ground almonds and
salt. Stir vigorously with a wooden spatula until the mixture becomes frothy
2 Sift in the flour all at once and mix rapidly with the spatula.
3 Take small pieces of the dough into your hands and flatten them between
