methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Roll the dough out on to a floured work surface. Wrap it around a rolling pin, then carefully unroll it over the tin. Adjust the dough once in the tin by lifting the edges.

Roll the rolling pin over the edge of the tin to cut off any excess dough. Follow these same steps for tartlet tins: line them up in a row with a little space between them before rolling out the dough.
Pierce the bottom of the dough with a fork.
Cover the bottom of the dough with nonstick baking paper and top it with baking beans (or dried beans). Bake for the time indicated by the recipe, then remove the weights and the paper.

recipes.searchText: Sweet Dough Baking workshop Ingredients 1 egg 40g icing sugar 2 tablespoons ground almonds A pinch of salt 110g plain flour + extra for dusting 60g butter, at room temperature, cut into very small pieces 1 In a large bowl, whisk the egg with the icing sugar, ground almonds and salt. Stir vigorously with a wooden spatula until the mixture becomes frothy and pale in colour. 2 Sift in the flour all at once and mix rapidly with the spatula. 3 Take small pieces of the dough into your hands and flatten them between your fingers. They shouldn’t stick together, but crumble into small pieces like breadcrumbs. 4 Turn the mixture on to a lightly floured surface. Scatter the pieces of butter on top of the dough, then knead it in by hand to incorporate it. Shape the dough into a ball. Wrap it in clingfilm and allow it to rest in the refrigerator Roll the dough out on to a floured work surface. Wrap it around a rolling pin, then carefully unroll it over the tin. Adjust the dough once in the tin by lifting the edges. Roll the rolling pin over the edge of the tin to cut off any excess dough. Follow these same steps for tartlet tins: line them up in a row with a little space between them before rolling out the dough. Pierce the bottom of the dough with a fork. Cover the bottom of the dough with nonstick baking paper and top it with baking beans (or dried beans). Bake for the time indicated by the recipe, then remove the weights and the paper.
recipes.title: Sweet Dough

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a heavy-based saucepan, combine the milk, measured water, salt, sugar and butter.
Bring to a boil, then sift in the flour all at once while mixing vigorously with a wooden spoon. Mix until the dough is smooth and even.
Over a low heat, cook down the mixture, stirring continuously, until it starts to come away from the sides of the saucepan.
Remove the saucepan from the heat, allow it to cool slightly, then add 1 egg, incorporating it using the wooden spoon.

Add the remaining eggs one by one, stirring vigorously and making sure each egg is mixed in completely before adding the next. Lift the mixture once in a while: when it drops off the spoon in a ribbon, it’s ready.
Put the batter in a piping bag with a smooth nozzle.
To make éclairs, pipe the batter onto a lined baking tray in 15cm-long strips.
To make choux pastries or religieuses, pipe 6cm dollops onto the tray. To make the small choux that go on top of the religieuses, or for chouquettes, pipe 3cm dollops.

recipes.searchText: Choux Pastry Baking workshop Ingredients 150ml milk 100ml water 1 level teaspoon salt 1 tablespoon caster sugar 100g butter 135g plain flour 4 eggs In a heavy-based saucepan, combine the milk, measured water, salt, sugar and butter. Bring to a boil, then sift in the flour all at once while mixing vigorously with a wooden spoon. Mix until the dough is smooth and even. Over a low heat, cook down the mixture, stirring continuously, until it starts to come away from the sides of the saucepan. Remove the saucepan from the heat, allow it to cool slightly, then add 1 egg, incorporating it using the wooden spoon. Add the remaining eggs one by one, stirring vigorously and making sure each egg is mixed in completely before adding the next. Lift the mixture once in a while: when it drops off the spoon in a ribbon, it’s ready. Put the batter in a piping bag with a smooth nozzle. To make éclairs, pipe the batter onto a lined baking tray in 15cm-long strips. To make choux pastries or religieuses, pipe 6cm dollops onto the tray. To make the small choux that go on top of the religieuses, or for chouquettes, pipe 3cm dollops.
recipes.title: Choux Pastry

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease and flour a 22cm round springform tin. In a large bowl, combine the eggs and the sugar. Place the bowl over a simmering bain-marie.

Whisk until the mixture has tripled in volume and reached 55–60°C (130– 140°F), a temperature that is still tolerable to the touch. Remove the bowl from the bain-marie and whip the mixture with an electric whisk until it has completely cooled.

Melt the butter and allow it to cool. Place 2 tablespoons of the previous mixture in a small bowl and incorporate the melted butter. Sift the flour into the large bowl, fold it into the egg–sugar mixture with a spatula, then carefully mix in the contents of the small bowl.
Pour the batter into the tin and bake for 35–40 minutes. Let the cake cool before removing it from the tin.

recipes.searchText: Genoese Sponge Cake Baking workshop Ingredients 4 eggs 140g caster sugar 40g butter + extra for greasing 140g plain flour + extra for dusting Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), Gas Mark 4. Grease and flour a 22cm round springform tin. In a large bowl, combine the eggs and the sugar. Place the bowl over a simmering bain-marie. Whisk until the mixture has tripled in volume and reached 55–60°C (130– 140°F), a temperature that is still tolerable to the touch. Remove the bowl from the bain-marie and whip the mixture with an electric whisk until it has completely cooled. Melt the butter and allow it to cool. Place 2 tablespoons of the previous mixture in a small bowl and incorporate the melted butter. Sift the flour into the large bowl, fold it into the egg–sugar mixture with a spatula, then carefully mix in the contents of the small bowl. Pour the batter into the tin and bake for 35–40 minutes. Let the cake cool before removing it from the tin.
recipes.title: Genoese Sponge Cake

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Combine the icing sugar and ground almonds and sift them on to a sheet of nonstick baking paper.
In a large bowl, whisk the egg whites with an electric whisk. Add the caster sugar in 3 stages to avoid deflating the beaten eggs. Continue to whisk until the mixture becomes a pliable meringue.
Pour in the ground almond mixture and carefully fold it in with a spatula.
Draw 2 circles on the baking paper. Put the batter into a piping bag fitted with a smooth 1cm nozzle and pipe the batter on to the baking paper in a spiral, starting from the centre, to make 2 discs.

recipes.searchText: Almond Dacquoise Baking workshop Ingredients 150g icing sugar 135g ground almonds 5 egg whites 50g caster sugar Line a baking tray with nonstick baking paper. Combine the icing sugar and ground almonds and sift them on to a sheet of nonstick baking paper. In a large bowl, whisk the egg whites with an electric whisk. Add the caster sugar in 3 stages to avoid deflating the beaten eggs. Continue to whisk until the mixture becomes a pliable meringue. Pour in the ground almond mixture and carefully fold it in with a spatula. Draw 2 circles on the baking paper. Put the batter into a piping bag fitted with a smooth 1cm nozzle and pipe the batter on to the baking paper in a spiral, starting from the centre, to make 2 discs.
recipes.title: Almond Dacquoise

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100g butter, at room temperature + extra for greasing

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl with the cocoa powder and baking powder. Separate the egg whites from the yolks. In a large bowl, whisk the butter with the egg yolks and sugars until creamy.
Add the sifted mixture and stir until the batter is smooth.
Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks and carefully fold them into the batter mixture with a spatula.
Grease and flour a springform tin and pour in the batter.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Sponge Cake Baking workshop Ingredients 180g plain flour + extra for dusting 30g cocoa powder 11g (2½ teaspoons) baking powder 6 eggs 100g butter, at room temperature + extra for greasing 100g caster sugar 7.5g (1 heaped teaspoon) vanilla sugar Sift the flour into a bowl with the cocoa powder and baking powder. Separate the egg whites from the yolks. In a large bowl, whisk the butter with the egg yolks and sugars until creamy. Add the sifted mixture and stir until the batter is smooth. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks and carefully fold them into the batter mixture with a spatula. Grease and flour a springform tin and pour in the batter.
recipes.title: Chocolate Sponge Cake

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 Genoese sponge cake, cooked in a rectangular tin

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Once the Genoese has cooled, dust a clean tea towel with icing sugar and place the sponge on top with the longer side perpendicular to you. Carefully peel away the baking paper.
Spread your icing over the Genoese leaving a 4cm margin, then top with mixed berries if desired.
Carefully roll the cake while holding it firmly and tucking it in neatly with the tea towel so as not to break it.
Refrigerate for 3 hours, keeping the roulade tightly wrapped until the time comes to decorate it and serve it. È Â È

recipes.searchText: How To Make A Swiss Roll Baking workshop Ingredients 1 Genoese sponge cake, cooked in a rectangular tin Icing sugar, for dusting Creamy icing of your choice 200g mixed berries (optional) Once the Genoese has cooled, dust a clean tea towel with icing sugar and place the sponge on top with the longer side perpendicular to you. Carefully peel away the baking paper. Spread your icing over the Genoese leaving a 4cm margin, then top with mixed berries if desired. Carefully roll the cake while holding it firmly and tucking it in neatly with the tea towel so as not to break it. Refrigerate for 3 hours, keeping the roulade tightly wrapped until the time comes to decorate it and serve it. È Â È
recipes.title: How To Make A Swiss Roll

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour, then quickly mix in the flour.
Bring the milk to the boil in a heavy-based saucepan.
Dilute the contents of the large bowl with a little of the boiling milk, then pour everything back into the saucepan while mixing continuously.
Cook over a very low heat, whisking continuously until the cream has thickened. Remove the saucepan from the heat and pour the cream into a bowl.

recipes.searchText: Crème Pâtissière Baking workshop Ingredients 3 egg yolks 50g caster sugar 20g plain flour 250ml whole milk In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until the mixture becomes pale in colour, then quickly mix in the flour. Bring the milk to the boil in a heavy-based saucepan. Dilute the contents of the large bowl with a little of the boiling milk, then pour everything back into the saucepan while mixing continuously. Cook over a very low heat, whisking continuously until the cream has thickened. Remove the saucepan from the heat and pour the cream into a bowl.
recipes.title: Crème Pâtissière

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To ensure the cream is very cold, pour it into a large bowl at least 1 hour before preparing the Chantilly cream and place it in the coldest part of the refrigerator. Take it out of the refrigerator just before using.
Lightly whip the cream by hand or with an electric whisk for 1 minute. Speed up the movement of the whisk (or electric handheld mixer) as the volume of the cream increases.
Add the sugars and continue to whisk. Stop whisking once the cream has doubled in volume and begins to stick to the whisk. Refrigerate until serving. È

recipes.searchText: Chantilly Cream Baking workshop Ingredients 500ml very cold whipping cream 30g icing sugar 7.5g (1 heaped teaspoon) vanilla sugar To ensure the cream is very cold, pour it into a large bowl at least 1 hour before preparing the Chantilly cream and place it in the coldest part of the refrigerator. Take it out of the refrigerator just before using. Lightly whip the cream by hand or with an electric whisk for 1 minute. Speed up the movement of the whisk (or electric handheld mixer) as the volume of the cream increases. Add the sugars and continue to whisk. Stop whisking once the cream has doubled in volume and begins to stick to the whisk. Refrigerate until serving. È
recipes.title: Chantilly Cream

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Split the half vanilla pod lengthways. In a heavy-based saucepan, bring the milk and vanilla pod to a boil, then remove it from the heat and let the vanilla infuse the milk for about 20 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks and sugar vigorously until the mixture becomes frothy and pale in colour.
Remove the vanilla pod from the milk and scrape the seeds out into the milk. Bring the milk to a boil again. Carefully whisk the boiling milk into the egg mixture.

Return the mixture to the saucepan and heat it over a very low heat, without bringing it to a boil, while stirring continuously until thickened. When you run your finger over the spatula and leave a trace, you’ll know you’ve reached the right consistency. Pour the crème anglaise into a large bowl or place the saucepan in a container filled with iced water to stop the cooking. Allow it to cool.

recipes.searchText: Crème Anglaise Baking workshop Ingredients ½ vanilla pod 500ml milk 6 egg yolks 60g caster sugar Split the half vanilla pod lengthways. In a heavy-based saucepan, bring the milk and vanilla pod to a boil, then remove it from the heat and let the vanilla infuse the milk for about 20 minutes. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks and sugar vigorously until the mixture becomes frothy and pale in colour. Remove the vanilla pod from the milk and scrape the seeds out into the milk. Bring the milk to a boil again. Carefully whisk the boiling milk into the egg mixture. Return the mixture to the saucepan and heat it over a very low heat, without bringing it to a boil, while stirring continuously until thickened. When you run your finger over the spatula and leave a trace, you’ll know you’ve reached the right consistency. Pour the crème anglaise into a large bowl or place the saucepan in a container filled with iced water to stop the cooking. Allow it to cool.
recipes.title: Crème Anglaise

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: In a large bowl, whip the egg whites into soft peaks with an electric handheld mixer and gradually add half the sugar.

Once the egg whites have doubled in volume, add half the remaining sugar and the vanilla extract (if using). Continue to whisk until the egg whites become stiff, smooth and shiny. Add the remaining sugar and mix well to incorporate. The mixture should be firm and stick to the whisk.

recipes.searchText: French Meringue Baking workshop Ingredients 5 egg whites 300g caster sugar 1 teaspoon vanilla extract (optional) In a large bowl, whip the egg whites into soft peaks with an electric handheld mixer and gradually add half the sugar. Once the egg whites have doubled in volume, add half the remaining sugar and the vanilla extract (if using). Continue to whisk until the egg whites become stiff, smooth and shiny. Add the remaining sugar and mix well to incorporate. The mixture should be firm and stick to the whisk.
recipes.title: French Meringue

How to top a tart with meringue

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare the meringue and spread it onto the top of the tart. You can also pipe it on in small rosettes.
Lightly brown the meringue with a blowtorch or put it under the grill for 2– 3 minutes.

recipes.searchText: Italian Meringue Baking workshop Ingredients 80g caster sugar 2 tablespoons water 2 egg whites 1 Bring the sugar and measured water to a boil in a small saucepan. Heat until the mixture reaches 120°C/248°F (a rolling boil: a bit of syrup dropped into cold water should form a very soft bead). 2 Meanwhile, begin to whip the egg whites. GOOD to know! • French meringue is a great base for vacherins or dry pastry cases that are flavoured and coloured. It’s also used to make tarts, baked Alaskas and ice cream floats. • Italian meringue is used to decorate the top of tarts that are then lightly browned in the oven or with a blowtorch. It can also be used to prepare mousses, sorbets or frozen soufflés. • Meringues can be flavoured with coffee extract, orange blossom water or lemon zest. recipes.title: Italian Meringue
recipes.yield: Makes enough for 1 tart or 6 tartlets

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 125g dark chocolate (at least 70 per cent cocoa solids), broken into pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Melt the dark chocolate over a barely simmering bain-marie, stirring with a wooden spoon.
Add the icing sugar, then the butter. Continue to stir until the mixture is smooth. Gradually stir in the measured water. Let it cool.
Place your cake on a wire rack over a large plate. When the icing has mostly cooled, pour it on top of the cake.
Smooth out the top and sides of the cake with a metal spatula.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Icing Baking workshop Ingredients 125g dark chocolate (at least 70 per cent cocoa solids), broken into pieces 80g icing sugar 60g butter, at room temperature 5 tablespoons cold water Melt the dark chocolate over a barely simmering bain-marie, stirring with a wooden spoon. Add the icing sugar, then the butter. Continue to stir until the mixture is smooth. Gradually stir in the measured water. Let it cool. Place your cake on a wire rack over a large plate. When the icing has mostly cooled, pour it on top of the cake. Smooth out the top and sides of the cake with a metal spatula.
recipes.title: Chocolate Icing

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: If you won’t be using chocolate coating pieces (known as chocolate ‘buttons’), break up the chocolate with a knife.
Melt half the chocolate over a bain-marie, without letting the water boil. If using white chocolate, remove the chocolate from the bain-marie as soon as the water starts to simmer.
Remove from the heat and add the remaining chocolate.
Whisk well. The chocolate lowers the temperature of the mixture, making it nice and shiny.

recipes.searchText: Tempered Chocolate Baking workshop Ingredients 300g chocolate of your choice If you won’t be using chocolate coating pieces (known as chocolate ‘buttons’), break up the chocolate with a knife. Melt half the chocolate over a bain-marie, without letting the water boil. If using white chocolate, remove the chocolate from the bain-marie as soon as the water starts to simmer. Remove from the heat and add the remaining chocolate. Whisk well. The chocolate lowers the temperature of the mixture, making it nice and shiny.
recipes.title: Tempered Chocolate

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Place the fruit in a large bowl with the sugar and lemon juice. Crush it in a blender, first pulsing, then continuously for 2–3 minutes until puréed and smooth.

Strain the purée while pressing down with a spatula in order to collect as much juice as possible. Gradually add the measured water, mixing as you go, until the coulis reaches the desired consistency.

recipes.searchText: Mixed Berry Coulis Baking workshop Ingredients 750g mixed berries (raspberries, redcurrants, strawberries, blackberries) 80g caster sugar 50ml lemon juice 100ml water Place the fruit in a large bowl with the sugar and lemon juice. Crush it in a blender, first pulsing, then continuously for 2–3 minutes until puréed and smooth. Strain the purée while pressing down with a spatula in order to collect as much juice as possible. Gradually add the measured water, mixing as you go, until the coulis reaches the desired consistency.
recipes.title: Mixed Berry Coulis

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200g dark chocolate (at least 70 per cent cocoa solids), broken into pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Place the chocolate in a large bowl over a saucepan filled with hot water. Gently melt the chocolate over the bain-marie while stirring with a wooden spoon. Add the butter to the chocolate and stir gently until the mixture is smooth and creamy.
Bring the milk to a boil in a small saucepan. Remove it from the heat and add the cream and sugar. Mix well with a whisk and bring it to a boil again.

Pour the contents of this saucepan over the chocolate mixture while whisking continuously until the mixture is smooth and even. Pour into a bowl or jug. Serve warm over ice cream or profiteroles, or allow it to cool and enjoy it with cake.

recipes.searchText: Chocolate Sauce Baking workshop Ingredients 200g dark chocolate (at least 70 per cent cocoa solids), broken into pieces 30g butter, cut into small pieces 200ml milk 2 tablespoons double cream 30g caster sugar Place the chocolate in a large bowl over a saucepan filled with hot water. Gently melt the chocolate over the bain-marie while stirring with a wooden spoon. Add the butter to the chocolate and stir gently until the mixture is smooth and creamy. Bring the milk to a boil in a small saucepan. Remove it from the heat and add the cream and sugar. Mix well with a whisk and bring it to a boil again. Pour the contents of this saucepan over the chocolate mixture while whisking continuously until the mixture is smooth and even. Pour into a bowl or jug. Serve warm over ice cream or profiteroles, or allow it to cool and enjoy it with cake.

lines: 6 unwaxed oranges with a thick rind

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring a saucepan full of water to a boil. Cut off both ends of the oranges. Score the orange rind 4 times from one end to the other with a small knife and peel away 4 equal-sized quarters. Boil them for 1 minute. Drain them in a sieve, then rinse them in cold water.

In a large saucepan, bring the measured water to a boil with the caster sugar and orange juice. Add the orange peel slices, cover and cook over a low heat for 1½ hours. Let the peel slices cool in the syrup overnight, then drain them on a wire rack. Let them dry out for 24 hours before storing them in a sealed container.

recipes.searchText: Crystallized Orange Peel Baking workshop Ingredients 6 unwaxed oranges with a thick rind 500ml water 500g caster sugar 100ml orange juice Bring a saucepan full of water to a boil. Add the orange peel slices, cover and cook over a low heat for 1½ hours. Let the peel slices cool in the syrup overnight, then drain them on a wire rack. ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 cake, already covered with icing or marzipan, according to the recipe

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Place the cake on a revolving plate (or on a serving plate). Knead the fondant icing to soften it (see here), roll it out as thinly as possible on a work surface dusted with icing sugar, then lay it on top of the cake.
Carefully smooth out the top by hand to make it nice and flat, then press the fondant icing down along the edges of the cake, carefully stretching it if necessary.
Cut off the excess fondant icing with a sharp knife.
Smooth out the sides of the cake with a plastic dough scraper.

recipes.searchText: How To Top A Cake with Fondant Icing Baking workshop Ingredients 1 cake, already covered with icing or marzipan, according to the recipe Fondant icing Icing sugar, for dusting Place the cake on a revolving plate (or on a serving plate).
